Headline: Mike Washington rushed nine times for 42 yards in the Raiders’ Week 11 loss to the Broncos.
News Snippet: Washington continued to operate as a change-of-pace back for the Raiders. He only saw two fewer carries than Ashton Jeanty, but the latter earned eight targets and led the team with 90 receiving yards. Washington was not targeted. Without any receiving work to fall back on, Washington is stuck in the RB4 ranks headed into a Week 12 matchup with Cleveland.

Headline: Quentin Johnston caught 1-of-2 targets for nine yards in the Chargers’ Week 11 loss to the Jets.
News Snippet: Johnston’s day was mostly quiet, although he did technically earn an end zone target on the Chargers’ sixth drive. The coaching staff tried to involve his post-catch skill set via a trick-play toss, but he was stuffed at the line of scrimmage. Johnston will be a shaky FLEX option against the Patriots next week, even if Justin Herbert clears the NFL’s concussion protocol.

Headline: Tre’ Harris caught 2-of-2 targets for 28 yards in the Chargers’ Week 11 loss to the Jets.
News Snippet: Harris snagged a 22-yard pass against busted coverage in this one, but that was not his most consequential play. On the Chargers’ third drive, Harris ran a go route inside the red zone and managed to get behind his coverage defender. Justin Herbert uncorked it, and Harris dove for it, but unfortunately, the pass bounced off his hands in the back of the end zone. Jets EDGE David Bailey committed a roughing the passer penalty on the play, which the Chargers accepted, erasing it from the box score. Harris is a boom-bust FLEX against the Patriots next week, pending Justin Herbert’s (concussion) availability.

Headline: Ashton Jeanty rushed 11 times for 79 yards in the Raiders’ Week 11 loss to the Broncos, adding five catches for 90 yards.
News Snippet: Jeanty broke his first carry of 20 or more yards on a 46-yard sprint into the red zone in the second quarter. The Raiders’ offensive line finally cleared a lane for the former No. 6 overall pick and he ran to daylight before being tracked down by a pair of Broncos defenders inside the five. Per Next Gen Stats, he hit 21.4 MPH on the run, which goes down as his highest top speed since being drafted. Jeanty was also productive through the air. His highlight of the day was a 68-yard receiving touchdown. He beat his man on a wheel route and Fernando Mendoza hit him in stride for a massive score. It was enough for Jeanty to lead the Raiders in receiving for the second straight week. Jeanty’s elite receiving role alone will keep him in the middle of the RB2 ranks for his Week 12 date with the Browns on Sunday Night Football.

Headline: Ladd McConkey caught 5-of-8 targets for 37 yards and two touchdowns in the Chargers’ Week 11 loss to the Jets.
News Snippet: McConkey mostly ran short-to-intermediate routes from the slot today. Although he dropped what might have been a first-down pickup on the first drive after halftime, he made the most of his other opportunities. McConkey scored an 11-yard touchdown via an out route early in the fourth quarter, faking an in-breaker that left his coverage defender in the dust. McConkey scored again with roughly two minutes left, shaking Jets LB DeMario Davis on a six-yard hitch-and-go before snagging Justin Herbert’s throw in the end zone. It was an encouraging performance for the Chargers’ No. 1 wide receiver. Unfortunately, the team announced post-game that Herbert has entered the NFL’s concussion protocol. If Herbert is active, McConkey will be back in the WR2 tier next week against the Patriots.

Headline: Braelon Allen rushed 16 times for 75 yards in the Jets’ Week 11 win over the Chargers, adding one reception for nine yards.
News Snippet: Allen racked up 17 touches in the No. 2 role behind featured starter Breece Hall. The Jets leaned heavily on their backfield today, with Geno Smith playing through an ankle injury. The coaching staff repeatedly called Allen’s number on multiple drives, allowing their burly backup to wear out Chargers defenders. Allen sealed the game with a 15-yard run up the middle, barreling through contact along the way. Allen must be rostered in all fantasy football formats as an elite bench stash at worst. He warrants FLEX consideration next week against the Dolphins.

Headline: Breece Hall rushed 20 times for 86 yards in the Jets’ Week 11 win over the Chargers, adding three receptions for 14 yards and one touchdown.
News Snippet: The Jets’ coaching staff designed a run-heavy game plan with Geno Smith (ankle) playing through an injury. Hall and Braelon Allen split 40 touches between the two of them. Although Allen should be expected to remain regularly involved, and even got a little work inside the Chargers’ 20-yard line, the Jets made sure Hall was in the game when they got near, or inside, the Chargers’ 10-yard line. Hall scored on 2nd-and-goal from the Chargers’ seven-yard line by running a route across the backfield, behind the line, before catching a pass in the flats and turning upfield for the score. Hall is an RB1 against the Dolphins in Week 12.

Headline: Fernando Mendoza completed 18-of-37 passes for 267 yards, three touchdowns, and an interception in the Raiders’ 38-24, Week 11 loss to the Broncos.
News Snippet: Mendoza got off to a dreadfully slow start. The Raiders’ first three drives amounted to 11 net yards and a trio of punts. Mendoza was already down 17 by the time he got the ball back for his fourth series. Mendoza then finally settled in and moved the ball well. His first career passing touchdown came on a well-thrown wheel route to Ashton Jeanty. He led his running back to space and Jeanty did the rest. Mendoza tossed two more scores in the second half, but his comeback bid came to a screeching halt with a fourth-quarter pick-six. Broncos corner Ja’Quan McMillan jumped the route and rather easily took the interception to the house. Things get much easier for Mendoza in Week 12 when he takes on the Browns next week. He will be near the back of the QB2 mix for his third start.

Headline: Mason Taylor caught 2-of-2 targets for 25 yards in the Jets’ Week 11 win over the Chargers.
News Snippet: Taylor made a nice, leaping grab for 19 yards on the Jets’ third drive before chipping in with a six-yarder on the next drive. He is a reliable starter in real life, but tougher to trust in fantasy football. He is a touchdown-dependent TE2 against the Dolphins next week.

Headline: Kenyon Sadiq caught 3-of-3 targets for 30 yards in the Jets’ Week 11 win over the Chargers.
News Snippet: The rookie tight end got going with a nine-yard catch between the hashes on the Jets’ second drive. He showed up again on the third drive, snagging a sidearm throw from Geno Smith behind the line of scrimmage before turning upfield and weaving through traffic for a 10-yard gain, bringing the offense into the red zone. He made a similar play on the fourth drive, taking a shallow crosser for 11 yards. Sadiq continues to flash intriguing post-catch traits while splitting time with Mason Taylor. Sadiq is stuck in the TE2 tier, but should play efficiently against the Dolphins next week.

Headline: Raiders coach Klint Kubiak said he is optimistic about Brock Bowers’ (ankle/quad) availability for Week 12 against the Browns.
News Snippet: Kubiak told reporters post-game that Bowers continues to make progress as he rehabs his two injuries. Bowers’ backup, Michael Mayer, caught just one pass for four yards today and picked up a back injury along the way. Hopefully, one or both of them will be good to go next week. Stay tuned.

Headline: Parker Washington caught 8-of-17 targets for 103 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 11 loss to the Giants.
News Snippet: Washington should have been credited with a touchdown on a gorgeous end zone throw from Trevor Lawrence but the refs for some reason called it incomplete after a lengthy replay review. This was the rare negative game script in which Parker could flex his statistical muscles as the Jags’ clear WR1, as the usually-balanced Jacksonville offense tilted pass heavy while chasing points in the second half. No other Jacksonville pass catcher had more than ten targets on the day. Washington will be an elite fantasy option in Week 12 against a wretched Titans secondary that gave up 152 yards and a touchdown to Parker in Week 10.

Headline: Isaiah Likely caught 1-of-3 targets for 35 yards in the Giants’ Week 11 win against the Jaguars.
News Snippet: Likely was invisible for most of the game and finished fourth in targets on the day. Along with most other New York pass catchers, Likely suffered from JJ McCarthy’s stunningly inefficient outing in which he was 15 percent below his expected completion rate and averaged a mere 4.6 yards per attempt. Better days will are likely ahead for the Giants tight end, including in Week 12 against the Colts.

Headline: Sterling Shepard caught 2-of-2 targets for 24 yards and two touchdowns in the Jets’ Week 11 win over the Chargers.
News Snippet: The Jets’ practice squad veteran seized the moment with Omar Cooper (ankle) and Isaiah Williams (ribs) sidelined today, scoring twice against the Chargers. The first was a sliding scramble-drill snag in the front of the end zone. On the second, Sterling ran a shallow crossing route from the right slot, caught the pass, turned upfield and simply outran Chargers CB Donte Jackson. Shepard is not on the FLEX radar next week against the Dolphins.

Headline: Bhayshul Tuten had ten rushes for 33 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 11 loss against the Giants, adding three catches for 20 yards.
News Snippet: Tuten came into the game with ankle and knee injuries and was hobbled throughout. He was spotted on the stationary bike a couple times in the first half and limped to the sideline a few times in the third quarter. Clearly nowhere close to 100 percent healthy, Tuten ceded five backfield touches to Chris Rodriguez, who was much more efficient with his opportunities (averaging seven yards per carry). The Jaguars could consider resting their lead back in Week 12 against the Titans. If he plays, Tuten will be a top-15 option.

Headline: Adonai Mitchell caught 2-of-3 targets for 30 yards in the Jets’ Week 11 win over the Chargers.
News Snippet: Mitchell bagged a 21-yard catch via a corner route on the opening drive. He should have bested it with a 40-plus-yard touchdown catch on the Jets’ fifth drive via another corner route, but Geno Smith overthrew him. Brutal. Mitchell’s downfield role lends itself to volatility, but there’s not much more he could have done there. He had his coverage defender beat. Mitchell remains a volatile yet capable FLEX option in Week 12 against the Dolphins.

Headline: Garrett Wilson caught 3-of-5 targets for 39 yards in the Jets’ Week 11 win over the Chargers.
News Snippet: Wilson generated a decent amount of his receiving yardage after the catch today. He spun off contact and broke another tackle on his 19-yard gain, and also added yards after the catch on a 12-yarder. His first incompletion was a shallow crosser on third down from the Chargers’ 32-yard line, which his coverage defender deserves credit for breaking up. The second incompletion was a desperation heave by Geno Smith under pressure from the Chargers’ six-yard line. The ball was badly overthrown to Wilson, just in front of the end zone, though. He had no chance of catching it. Wilson is a WR2 against the Dolphins in Week 12.

Headline: Geno Smith completed 17-of-21 passes for 176 yards and three touchdowns in the Jets’ 27-24, Week 11 win over the Chargers.
News Snippet: The Jets dialed up a run-heavy game plan with Smith playing through an ankle injury suffered last weekend. The ailment didn’t stop Smith from playing efficiently against the Chargers, though. Smith linked up with Breece Hall and Sterling Shepard (twice) for touchdowns today. Smith overthrew Adonai Mitchell on what could have been a 40-plus-yard end zone target, but luckily, Breece Hall ripped off a 26-yarder that set up one of Smith’s touchdown passes to Shepard, who was elevated from the practice squad this week. Smith warrants QB2 treatment against the Dolphins in Week 12.

Headline: Makai Lemon caught 1-of-3 targets for one yard in the Eagles’ Week 11 win against the Steelers.
News Snippet: Lemon was a distant afterthought in the Philly offense with DeVonta Smith returning from a hamstring injury and leading the team with 12 targets (57 percent target share). Lemon should not be rostered in most fantasy leagues for the remainder of the season unless Smith again misses time.

Headline: Justin Herbert completed 15-of-21 passes for 131 yards and two touchdowns in the Chargers’ 24-27, Week 11 loss to the Jets, adding eight rushes for 32 yards and one touchdown.
News Snippet: Immediately after the game, the Chargers announced that Herbert had entered the NFL’s concussion protocol. He took six sacks and eight hits, including one that resulted in a roughing-the-passer penalty after David Bailey hit him in the facemask while trying to disrupt a pass. Bailey had a field day aside from that, registering two quarterback hits and two sacks while forcing a fumble during one of the latter plays. Fortunately for Herbert, an offensive lineman recovered possession. Herbert’s connection with Ladd McConkey improved as the game progressed, leading to two fourth-quarter touchdown passes. Herbert also audibled to a quarterback-keeper from the Jets’ 10-yard line earlier in the game, which he successfully converted for a score. He notably had his left index finger taped up after halftime. If active next week against the Patriots, Herbert will be a high-end QB2. He is backed up by DJ Uiagalelei.

Headline: Jake Elliott made all four of his field goal attempts in the Eagles’ Week 11 win against the Steelers.
News Snippet: Elliott also made his lone extra point attempt in the victory. Elliott drilled a couple long kicks through the wind in Philadelphia as he continued a solid 2026 campaign. He’s made 11 of his 12 field goal tries on the season. Sunday marked the first time in 2026 in which Elliott made more than two field goal attempts in a game. He’ll be a decent fantasy option in Week 12 against Dallas.

Headline: Vikings declared QB Kyler Murray, WR Jordan Addison, CB Isaiah Rodgers, QB Max Brosmer, and S Jay Ward inactive for Week 11 against the 49ers.
News Snippet: Addison will miss his second consecutive game while the team gets Jauan Jennings back from his own two-game absence. Expect Tai Felton and Myles Price to fill in for Addison while addition volume remains most likely to concentrate on Justin Jefferson and T.J. Hockenson.

Headline: Mike Evans (Achilles) is active for Week 11 against the Vikings.
News Snippet: Evans returns from three missed games due to an aggravation of the Achilles injury that has plagued him throughout the season, and while he could see his snaps and routes managed, he brings a fantasy WR2 profile to the table in a difficult matchup against the Vikings. Fantasy managers likely did not start him considering the timing of the game this week, hoping he simply makes it through Week 11 healthy. Inactive for the 49ers are QB Kurtis Rourke, OT Enrique Cruz, DE Khalid Kareem, WR Demarcus Robinson, and LB Dre Greenlaw.

Headline: Adam Butler (concussion) will not return to the Raiders’ Week 11 game against the Broncos.
News Snippet: Fellow defensive tackle Tim Keenan (knee) is also done for the day. The Raiders were already one of the best matchups for running backs entering Week 11. Expect the Broncos to lean on Jonah Coleman to close this game out.

Headline: Gunnar Helm caught 2-of-3 targets for 14 yards in the Titans’ Week 11 loss to the Cowboys.
News Snippet: 14 of Helm’s 23 catches on the year have come in the past four weeks. It’s been a good start for a second-year pro trying to create some TE2 relevance but not really enough, even in a down year for the position. With all 32 teams active for Week 12 and bye weeks lingering on for only two more Sundays after that, Helm is facing long odds of becoming 12-team league relevant.

Headline: Elic Ayomanor caught 3-of-3 targets for 27 yards in the Titans’ Week 11 loss to the Cowboys.
News Snippet: The three-catch effort was Ayomanor’s fourth straight, though he has exceeded three just once during that timespan. He is also averaging only 46 yards in the process, and has not found the end zone. Translation, Ayomanor’s play has been better, but not better enough you are seriously considering him as a WR4. That is especially true for slates like Week 12 where all 32 teams will be active.

Headline: Calvin Ridley caught 5-of-6 targets for 68 yards and a touchdown in the Titans’ Week 11 loss to the Cowboys.
News Snippet: Ridley entered the game with only six catches for 91 scoreless yards on the season, so he nearly doubled his 2026 production. The highlight was a 12-yard touchdown in garbage time that just happened to be one of the most insane throws of the year. Rolling near the sideline, Cam Ward made a cross-field, cross-body pass to find Ridley on the opposite side of the field in the end zone. It was an easy catch. Good stuff, though nearly all of Ridley’s production came with the Titans down multiple scores in the fourth quarter. The offense is playing better, but not better enough that Ridley is set to return to 12-team league relevance.

Headline: Darius Cooper caught 4-of-5 targets for 59 yards in the Eagles’ Week 11 win against the Steelers.
News Snippet: Cooper led all Eagles pass catchers in catches and receiving yards on a day that saw Joe Milton throw just 21 passes in a run-heavy game. Cooper played a full-time role because Dontayvian Wicks remained sidelined after practicing over the past week. Cooper would profile as an interesting flex play next week against Dallas if Wicks remains out.

Headline: Juwan Johnson failed to catch his lone target in the Saints’ Week 11 loss to the Bears.
News Snippet: Johnson saw just one target before exiting in the second half of the Saints’ Week 11 game against the Bears. He did not return to the game and head coach Kellen Moore said the 30-year-old is still being evaluated with a hamstring injury. Johnson has not exceeded three targets for five straight weeks now. He can remain on waiver wires moving forward, though Noah Fant enters the streaming conversation if Johnson misses any time.

Headline: Chimere Dike caught 6-of-7 targets for 69 yards in the Titans’ Week 11 loss to the Cowboys.
News Snippet: Dike notched a 22-yard gain on a flea flicker on the Titans’ first play from scrimmage and went on to lead the team in receiving as it put up 30 points in a road loss. Good stuff, and Dike’s second pop-up effort in as many weeks, though it was Carnell Tate and Calvin Ridley who made the biggest plays. Second-year fourth-rounder Dike has been one of the biggest beneficiaries as fellow sophomore Cam Ward has finally started to play better, but he’s still having a difficult time cracking the top 48 at receiver. That is going to be especially true for Week 12 against the Jaguars as we get a rare November week with all 32 teams actually playing football.

Headline: Noah Fant caught 2-of-5 targets for 19 yards in the Saints’ Week 11 loss to the Bears.
News Snippet: Fant was the Saints’ leading tight end on the day, seeing the most snaps, targets, and receptions in the tight end room. He saw a pair of red zone targets in the fourth quarter, though Tyler Shough could not connect with him and the drive ended in a turnover-on-downs. Juwan Johnson is his primary receiving competition, but Johnson saw just one target before exiting with a hamstring injury. No Saints tight end needs to be started for fantasy purposes at this point; Fant is in the streaming tight end conversation should Johnson miss any time.

Headline: Ted Hurst caught 5-of-7 targets for 56 yards and two touchdowns in the Bucs’ Week 11 loss to the Lions.
News Snippet: Hurst brought down a beautiful deep shot right in the bread basket with four seconds left on the clock in the second quarter. He double-dipped near the end of the fourth quarter with a quick out at the goal line for his second touchdown of the day. Hurst led the Bucs in all receiving categories, including a 21 percent target share. Hurst has been a boom/bust receiver this year who mostly gives fantasy managers busts, but his Week 11 breakout gives him something to build on. He will be a high-risk FLEX play when the Bucs take on the Panthers next week.

Headline: Devaughn Vele caught 7-of-7 targets for 76 yards in the Saints’ Week 11 loss to the Bears.
News Snippet: Vele saw a decrease in opportunities last week with Jordyn Tyson’s activation off injured reserve. However, Tyson saw limited usage in Week 11 against the Bears, with Vele leading Saints receivers in snaps and ranking second in targets, receptions, and yards. Fantasy managers should wait to see if Tyson has any injury limitations moving forward, but Vele would be back in the WR3/4 ranks if Tyson is limited for Week 12 against the Bengals.

Headline: Brevyn Spann-Ford caught 2-of-2 targets for five yards and a touchdown in the Cowboys’ Week 11 win over the Titans.
News Snippet: The closest thing the Cowboys have to a No. 1 tight end during Jake Ferguson’s ongoing absence, Spann-Ford’s two-yard touchdown in the fourth quarter was just the second of his career. It’s what got the Cowboys to 50 points, which is both cool and also tells you all you need to know about Spann-Ford’s fantasy value. It took the Cowboys running it up late against one of the worst teams in the league for Spann-Ford to find the paint. He remains outside the top 30 in the weekly tight end rankings.

Headline: Ryan Flournoy caught an 11-yard pass in the Cowboys’ Week 11 win over the Titans.
News Snippet: Flournoy had his season-worst outing as the Cowboys had their season-best scoring effort. Go figure. Flournoy’s 11-yard grab came on the opening series only for him to draw zero more targets. That’s a rough development for WR3 desperados with six teams on bye. It is also a faceplant that is unlikely to repeat on Thanksgiving Day against the Eagles even with CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens posting crazy usage numbers. The problem for Flournoy is, with all 32 teams active for Week 12, there’s simply no real way to get him into fantasy lineups.

Headline: Jordan Tyson caught 1-of-2 targets for 6 yards in the Saints’ Week 11 loss to the Bears, adding one carry for four yards.
News Snippet: Tyson saw the first offensive touch for the Saints, getting four-yard carry to start things off. He saw just one more touch the rest of the game and was barely on the field for the Saints’ final offensive drive. Though he was cleared off the injury report heading into the weekend, Tyson was dealing with a chest injury last week. Also coming back from a hamstring injury this season, Tyson’s compounding injury list may have played a role in him seeing just half of the offensive snaps against the Bears after getting 13 targets last week. He saw just two targets as Chris Olave took the alpha receiver role back. Fantasy managers should monitor Tyson’s injury status heading into Week 12; he is in the WR3 ranks against the Bengals next week.

Headline: Emeka Egbuka caught 2-of-5 targets for 18 yards in the Bucs’ Week 11 loss to the Lions.
News Snippet: There’s not much to say here. It’s just not happening for Egbuka this year. He’s struggling to earn targets and doing nothing when the ball comes his way. Ted Hurst broke out with two scores and 56 yards on a team-high 56 yards today. Egbuka watched on with a measly 15 percent target share. He’s averaging a dismal five yards per target and has forced zero missed tackles. Egbuka will tumble into the WR4 ranks for his Week 12 game against Carolina. With no teams on bye, fantasy managers can feel comfortable sending him to the bench next week.

Headline: Darnell Washington caught all three of his targets for 22 yards in the Steelers’ Week 11 loss to the Eagles.
News Snippet: Washington again ran fewer pass routes than Pat Freiermuth, who caught all five of his targets on the day. Washington won’t have much in the way of fantasy value until or unless Freiermuth misses time. Washington has five games this season with at least three catches.

Headline: Dallas Goedert caught his only target for 38 yards in the Eagles’ Week 11 win against the Steelers.
News Snippet: Goedert ran a pass route on 20 of the team’s 29 drop backs but only saw one look from Joe Milton, who attempted a meager 21 passes and threw for 141 scoreless yards. DeVonta Smith’s return to the Eagles lineup netted him a 57 percent target share. That kind of target domination won’t leave much opportunity for anyone else, including Goedert, who should not be played in 12-team formats for now. The Eagles play the Cowboys in Week 12.

Headline: Javonte Williams rushed 18 times for 67 yards and a touchdown in the Cowboys’ Week 11 win over the Titans, adding three receptions for 24 yards and a second score.
News Snippet: Williams lost some mop-up work to someone named Jashaun Corbin but cleared 20 touches for the fourth time in five games. The touchdowns were his 11th and 12th of the season, and give him 25 in 27 appearances as a Cowboy. Williams continues to not provide efficiency, but that’s not what’s needed opposite the Cowboys’ elite receiver duo. Williams needs to finish drives at the goal line and do a little bit of everything else, and that’s what he has been doing. Williams will be a low-end RB1 for Thanksgiving Day against the Eagles.

Headline: CJ Donaldson rushed one time for five yards in the Saints’ Week 11 loss to the Bears, adding four receptions for 12 yards and a fumble.
News Snippet: Donaldson is head coach Kellen Moore’s pride and joy as a passing-down back in the backfield. The undrafted rookie continues to run routes despite a lack of efficiency and production all season. He was used as a pass blocker and ran 25 routes on the day, more than rookie wideout Jordyn Tyson. Donaldson fumbled on one of his receptions in the second quarter, totaling 12 yards through the air and five on the ground. He has no fantasy value heading into Week 12.

Headline: Chris Godwin caught all three of his targets for 13 yards in the Bucs’ Week 11 loss to the Lions.
News Snippet: The Bucs leaned on Godwin on third downs, using him to move the chains on two of his three targets. That, however, is a cold comfort for fantasy managers. Godwin hasn’t hit 50 yards in a game this year and is still looking for his first touchdown. If you somehow made it this far into the season with Godwin on your roster, it’s past time to cut bait. He’s somewhere beyond the WR5 ranks heading into Week 12.

Headline: Will Shipley had four rushes for nine yards in the Eagles’ Week 11 win against the Steelers.
News Snippet: Shipley saw some decent fourth quarter run with Saquon Barkley nursing some sort of left arm injury. Shipley would likely take over the Eagles’ lead back if Barkley were to miss time. He should be rostered in most 12-team formats just in case, considering the Eagles take on the Cowboys in Week 12.

Headline: Pat Freiermuth caught all five of his targets for 39 yards in the Steelers’ Week 11 loss to the Eagles.
News Snippet: Freiermuth ran 33 routes on the day while Darnell Washington logged 22 routes and had three targets from Aaron Rodgers. Freiermuth was fourth on the team in targets and receiving yards. Sunday was only the fourth time this season Freiermuth had more than four catches in a game. His waning route participation and the run heaviness of the Pittsburgh offense make Freiermuth nothing more than a desperation option for Week 12 against Denver.

Headline: Tony Pollard rushed 21 times for 110 yards in the Titans’ Week 11 loss to the Cowboys.
News Snippet: Pollard was held without a catch on one target. Frustrating, though fantasy managers will take Pollard’s third 100-yard rushing effort in four weeks considering the Titans were down 27-9 at halftime. Pollard was “keeping the defense honest” as Cam Ward again showed increased play-making ability in the passing game. Pollard has now cleared 75 yards from scrimmage in five straight contests after doing so just once in the first five games of the season. He is amongst a number of Titans just genuinely playing better, though it is still not translating to victories. That will remain a pipe dream for Week 12, but Pollard will be rematching with a Jaguars defense he got for 99 yards from scrimmage in Week 10. It must be noted that was due in large part to a ridiculous eight receptions, which probably won’t be repeated seeing as Pollard has only 22 on the year.

Headline: Alvin Kamara rushed one time for one yard in the Saints’ Week 11 loss to the Bears, adding one reception for one yard and a touchdown.
News Snippet: Kamara was the third running back in the Saints backfield, seeing just six total snaps. He came in for a fourth-and-goal pay at the one-yard line and caught a Tyler Shough pass for the touchdown. Kamara only received one carry for one yard. The Saints have a frustrating backfield committee, with Travis Etienne getting the bulk of the carries, CJ Donaldson running routes, and Kamara coming in for the occasional red zone target. Three touchdowns in his last two games keeps Kamara on the fantasy radar, though he is close to a zero without the red zone opportunities. Kamara is best left on benches for Week 12 against the Bengals.

Headline: Travis Etienne rushed 14 times for 76 yards in the Saints’ Week 11 loss to the Bears.
News Snippet: The good news is that Etienne started the game for the Saints backfield and received 14-of-16 running back carries. He led the backfield with 21 total snaps as Audric Estime was a healthy scratch against the Bears. Etienne’s best run of the day was a 46-yard carry in the second quarter, where he was chased down and tackled inside the five-yard line. He got two more opportunities and got the ball to the one-yard line, but did not get the touchdown on that drive. Etienne’s lack of passing-game usage and Alvin Kamara’s involvement as a touchdown scorer caps Etienne’s ceiling for fantasy purposes. He belongs in the RB3 ranks for Week 12 against the Bengals.

Headline: Cade Otton caught 1-of-3 targets for eight yards in the Bucs’ Week 11 loss to the Lions.
News Snippet: Otton popped up with a four-catch, eight-target game before the Bucs’ Week 10 bye. He was unable to build on that box score and all but disappeared today. Otton hasn’t topped five catches or 56 yards in a game this year. He has also been held without a touchdown through nearly three months of action. He’s barely even a TE2 for Week 12 against the Panthers.

Headline: George Pickens caught 7-of-10 targets for 102 yards and a touchdown in the Cowboys’ Week 11 win over the Titans.
News Snippet: Pickens got off to a slow start this afternoon, seeming to not finish a route or two, but finished molten hot. He is now up to 18 catches for 247 yards and four touchdowns on 28 targets over the past two weeks. Ridiculous numbers, though somewhat sustainable in this narrow, explosive offense. For Thanksgiving Day he will be rematching with an Eagles defense he got for 4/57/1 last month. The Eagles have moved on to their No. 3 quarterback since then and traded a few key contributors. Even with all 32 teams active for Week 12, Pickens will remain in the low-end WR1 mix.

Headline: Kenneth Gainwell rushed four times for 16 yards in the Bucs’ Week 11 loss to the Lions, adding four catches for 43 yards.
News Snippet: Bucs coach Todd Bowles told reporters on Monday that Gainwell could see more touches going forward to help keep Bucky Irving fresh. That couldn’t have been further from the truth today as Irving out-touched Gainwell 21-8. Gainwell did, however, post his second-best receiving line of the year. His only better game came two weeks ago, before Tampa’s bye, against the Bears. Gainwell might finally be developing a receptions-based floor, but a two-game sample can’t be taken as gospel. Gainwell will remain on the RB3/4 border when he takes on the Panthers next week.

Headline: Zavion Thomas caught 2-of-3 targets for 56 yards and a touchdown in the Bears’ Week 11 win over the Saints, adding one carry for 30 yards.
News Snippet: Thomas was the subject of multiple explosive plays against the Saints. He saw just offensive 10 snaps, but Ben Johnson schemed up multiple plays to utilize the rookie receiver’s speed. A 40-yard reception in the third quarter and 30-yard rush in the second quarter highlighted a career-best day for Thomas. He is still not fantasy relevant, but his usage should be monitored as the Bears scheme up more plays for him.

Headline: Jaylen Warren had nine rushes for 28 yards in the Steelers’ Week 11 loss to the Eagles, adding two catches for one yard.
News Snippet: Warren was snuffed out by a swarming Philadelphia defense that appeared committed to stopping the Pittsburgh rushing attack and forcing Aaron Rodgers to beat them (he did not). Warren ran 36 routes on the day to Rico Dowdle’s 16 routes, though it was Dowdle who led the backfield with five targets. Warren now has back-to-back down games in a collapsing Steelers offense. Things won’t get much easier in Week 12 against the Broncos.

Headline: Rico Dowdle had five rushes for 15 yards in the Steelers’ Week 11 loss to the Eagles, adding four catches for 19 yards.
News Snippet: Jaylen Warren, meanwhile, managed 29 yards on nine rushing attempts and caught one of his two targets. Dowdle got quite a lot of second half playing time, finishing the game with 16 pass routes to 36 routes for Warren. Dowdle is good for 7-10 touches per week in the low-octane Pittsburgh offense, making him a desperation flex option in deeper formats.

Headline: Kalif Raymond caught 1-of-4 targets for 14 yards in the Bears’ Week 11 win over the Saints.
News Snippet: Raymond was targeted four times, including an incomplete end zone target on fourth down in the first half. He caught one of his targets for 14 total yards, though he had the second-most wide receiver snaps on the team. Raymond is still involved as the starting outside receiver opposite Rome Odunze but has boom-or-bust WR5 viability at best heading into Week 12

Headline: Justice Hill rushed six times for 69 yards and a touchdown in the Ravens’ Week 11 loss to the Panthers, adding four receptions for 27 additional yards.
News Snippet: Hill fell victim to one of the worst rules in football when he fumbled inside the Panthers’ five-yard line on a 36-yard run and watched the ball run out of the end zone. The turnover resulted in a touchback that rewarded the Panthers with the ball at Baltimore’s 20-yard line, but Hill would get his revenge on the following drive when he ran in a 19-yard touchdown to put the Ravens up 26-22 before halftime. Despite the gaffe early in the game, Hill was very efficient in this one, averaging a solid 9.6 yards per touch while being a difference-maker both on the ground and through the air. He has now seen double-digit opportunities in four straight weeks, but he remains difficult to trust as anything more than an RB4/Flex play, especially with Derrick Henry around to vulture any short-yardage touchdowns.

Headline: Baker Mayfield completed 20-of-33 passes for 187 yards and two touchdowns in the Bucs’ 31-21, Week 11 loss to the Lions.
News Snippet: Mayfield appeared to be unlikely to suit up for today’s game when the week started, but a pair of limited practices was enough to get him on the field today. Things got off to a scary start when he was crushed for a sack-fumble on his first dropback of the day. He would go on to take four sacks for a total loss of 33 yards. Somehow, Mayfield looked more than willing as a runner, adding 36 yards on six carries. It was ultimately a solid fantasy outing from Mayfield, assisted by a garbage-time touchdown to Ted Hurst. A date with the Panthers next week will keep Mayfield in the QB2 mix next week, but he’s far from the best streaming option available to most fantasy managers.

Headline: Mitchell Evans caught 5-of-5 targets for 44 yards and a touchdown in the Panthers’ Week 11 win over the Ravens.
News Snippet: It was a career day for Evans, who posted career highs in targets, catches, and receiving yards, and scored his third touchdown as a pro in the first quarter. Evans caught a 23-yard touchdown pass from Bryce Young on a trick play that began with a direct snap to Jalen Coker, fighting through contact near the goal line to extend his arms across for the score. Evans’ production was impressive for a player who ran only 12 routes, per the early PFF data. That said, his low involvement should caution fantasy managers considering him as a streaming option after scouting the box score. Evans is best left on waivers heading into Week 12 against the Buccaneers.

Headline: Jalen Coker caught 4-of-7 targets for 47 yards in the Panthers’ Week 11 win over the Ravens.
News Snippet: Coker’s biggest play of the game came on a 35-yard reception in the first quarter, which precluded a 23-yard touchdown pass to tight end Mitchell Evans on the following play. Coker would muster just 12 yards on his other three catches, as he was used primarily in the short and intermediate areas of the field. He took a hard hit from Ravens LB Roquan Smith late in the fourth quarter and was placed in the league’s concussion protocol. Assuming he remains in the league’s concussion protocol on Monday, Coker will need to clear several hurdles if he hopes to suit up for Week 12 against the Buccaneers on Monday Night Football.

Headline: Tetairoa McMillan caught 6-of-9 targets for 71 yards and a touchdown in the Panthers’ Week 11 win over the Ravens.
News Snippet: McMillan has scored twice in his last three games and led the Panthers in both targets and receptions in this one. His lone score came on a seven-yard pass from Bryce Young in the second quarter, but it could have been a much bigger day for McMillan were it not for an interception by Young in the third quarter. Young attempted to find McMillan again in the end zone in the third quarter, but a diving interception by Ravens CB T.J. Tampa ended any hopes of points for McMillan. McMillan has gone for 50-plus yards in three of his last four games and will be a strong WR2 in Week 12’s game against the Buccaneers.

Headline: CeeDee Lamb caught 11-of-12 targets for 132 yards and a touchdown in the Cowboys’ Week 11 win over the Titans.
News Snippet: Lamb’s fifth 100-yard effort of the season and second in three weeks put him above 1,000 yards for the sixth consecutive season, good for a new Cowboys franchise record. Simply abusing overmatched Titans CB Cor’Dale Flott, it is barely an exaggeration to say Lamb was open at will against the Titans’ overmatched defense. The Eagles will be a slightly tougher Thanksgiving Day matchup, but not by much. Enjoy the holiday with your WR1.

Headline: Carnell Tate caught 2-of-5 targets for 58 yards and a touchdown in the Titans’ Week 11 loss to the Cowboys.
News Snippet: Active for the first time since Week 7, the No. 4 overall pick caught a -1 yard pass in the first quarter before adding a 59-yard touchdown in the third. In between, he drew a 38-yard DPI in the end zone to set the Titans up at the one-yard line. On his score, Tate appeared to be down by contact near mid-field, but he realized he had not been touched and got up and sprinted to the end zone. Heady stuff, though we would have liked to see more targets. Tate thankfully avoided setbacks with his shoulder injury, and is now ready to slot into the WR24-30 range for a tough Week 12 matchup with the Jags. Tate would be a safer WR2 were it not a 32-team slate for the holiday week.

Headline: Jared Goff completed 20-of-28 passes for 279 yards and two touchdowns in the Lions’ 31-21, Week 11 win over the Bucs.
News Snippet: A long Bucs drive limited the Lions to one possession in the first quarter. Jake Bates missed his field goal try, resulting in a slow start for Detroit. They shook the rust off in the second quarter and cruised past the Bucs over the next three frames. Because Tampa’s offense didn’t put up much of a fight, Goff’s passing volume was limited once again. He hasn’t thrown for more than 32 passes in a game since Week 4. The good news for fantasy managers is that the Lions take on the Bears in what should be a Thanksgiving afternoon shootout next week. Goff topped 330 yards in both of his games against the Bears last year. He will be a top-half QB1 for Week 12.

Headline: Rome Odunze caught 4-of-4 targets for 45 yards in the Bears’ Week 11 win over the Saints.
News Snippet: Odunze was involved in the intermediate area for the Bears, making a 19-yard grab on the first drive. He made a 16-yard catch later in the first half, getting tackled inside the five-yard line and setting up a touchdown. His four targets were tied for the most on the team, with Caleb Williams only attempting 23 passes against the Saints. Odunze’s downfield targets keep him in the FLEX conversation for fantasy purposes. He is in the WR3/FLEX ranks for Week 12 against the Lions.

Headline: Mark Andrews caught 2-of-3 targets for 14 yards in the Ravens’ Week 11 loss to the Panthers.
News Snippet: Andrews’ disappointing performance comes a week after he caught eight targets for 82 yards in Jacoby Brissett’s debut with the Ravens. The Ravens worked to get all three tight ends involved in this one, as Andrews, Matthew Hibner, and Josh Cuevas combined to get eight targets, with Andrews and Cuevas both getting three looks. Andrews’ promising performance against the Chargers gave fantasy managers a reason to hope for more this week, especially with six teams on bye. With all 32 teams playing in Week 12, it’s safe to say Andrews shouldn’t be treated as anything more than a desperation play on the road against the Texans.

Headline: Rashod Bateman caught 2-of-6 targets for 67 yards and a touchdown in the Ravens’ Week 11 loss to the Panthers.
News Snippet: Bateman’s touchdown pass came on a play from the wildcat that started with Derrick Henry receiving the snap. While Henry handed the ball off to Justice Hill, who then pitched to Jacoby Brissett, Bateman streaked down the field, leaving every member of the Panthers’ secondary in the dust as they attempted to dissect the trick play called by Ravens OC Declan Doyle. Brissett delivered a slightly underthrown ball to Bateman, but it proved inconsequential given the distance between Bateman and the nearest defender. The 26-year-old receiver hauled in the pass without any trouble and made his way into the end zone to give the Ravens an early 9-0 lead. Bateman would only catch one more pass the rest of the day, but his six targets now give him 11 in his two games with Brissett under center. While it’s hard to imagine Bateman having any reliable fantasy value this season, he could be worth a desperation dart throw in deeper leagues in Week 12 against the Texans.

Headline: Zay Flowers caught 8-of-11 targets for 97 yards in the Ravens’ Week 11 loss to the Panthers.
News Snippet: In two games with Jacoby Brissett, Flowers has caught 14-of-18 targets for 171 scoreless yards. This is great news for fantasy managers, who saw Flowers’ fantasy value in the tank when the duo of Tyler Huntley and Joe Fagnano led him to just six yards over a two-week stretch. Brissett’s arrival has been good news for Flowers, who ripped off two gains of 20-plus yards on the afternoon and led the Ravens in both targets and receiving yards. He will be a high-end WR2 next week against a Texans secondary that has proven vulnerable this season.

Headline: Luther Burden caught 2-of-3 targets for 10 yards in the Bears’ Week 11 win over the Saints, adding one carry for three yards.
News Snippet: Burden had little involvement in a low-volume passing day for the Bears. He saw three of Caleb Williams’ 23 passing attempts on a day where no Bears pass-catcher had more than four targets. Rookie Zavion Thomas saw the splash plays on the day as Burden had short-yardage usage to pick up quick first downs out of the slot. The first half game script did not favor Burden, but given his elite production in recent weeks, he is back in the low-end WR2 ranks for a Thanksgiving day game against the Lions.

Headline: Amon-Ra St. Brown caught 5-of-6 targets for 37 yards and a touchdown in the Lions’ Week 11 win over the Bucs.
News Snippet: With only 28 attempts for Jared Goff, there simply wasn’t much receiving work to go around. St. Brown still led the Lions in targets alongside Sam LaPorta. Despite the quiet day, fantasy managers will be satisfied with St. Brown’s eighth touchdown of the year. He scored No. 8 on an easy strike over the middle of the field from 14 yards out. With a shootout versus the Bears scheduled for Thanksgiving, St. Brown is set for elite fantasy numbers in Week 12.

Headline: Cam Ward completed 21-of-30 passes for 248 yards and two touchdowns in the Titans’ 51-30, Week 11 loss to the Cowboys, adding two rushes for three yards and a third score.
News Snippet: Recalled from fantasy benches for streamer duties vs. the defense-less Cowboys, Ward had his first three-score game of the year. It was also his third straight multi-score effort after managing just one in first seven starts. No. 3 was a 12-yard garbage time connection with Calvin Ridley, but that description doesn’t really do it justice. Flushed from the pocket and seemingly running out of bounds, Ward instead made like prime Aaron Rodgers and threw the ball across his body, across the middle of the field into Ridley’s arms like it was a loaf of bread. It was the most impressive play of his young NFL career, and an exclamation point on his recent improved play. Today was a soft matchup, but that was not the case for the Jaguars in Week 10, with whom Ward must now rematch in Week 12. Despite his hot streak, Ward will find himself outside the top 20 for Thanksgiving week because of his tough setup and all 32 teams being active for the holiday slate.

Headline: The Baltimore Banner’s Giana Han reports Derrick Henry cleared concussion protocol after Week 11’s loss to the Panthers.
News Snippet: Henry didn’t return to the field after exiting in the fourth quarter to be evaluated for a concussion, but it was reportedly shortly after that he cleared the league’s concussion protocol. Henry rushed 13 times for 94 yards and a touchdown in Sunday’s loss while catching another four passes for 17 yards. Barring any setback, we would expect him to be good to go for Week 12’s game against the Texans.

Headline: Tyler Bass converted on 4-of-5 field goal attempts in the Bills’ Week 11 win over the Dolphins.
News Snippet: Bass was the beneficiary of the Bills’ offense continuing to stall out once they got into the Dolphins’ territory. Bass made field goals of 43, 54, 40, and 28 yards on the day. However, the 29-year-old did miss a 54-yarder in the third quarter, which was his first missed field goal of the season. He’s now 24-of-25 on the season after missing all of last year with an injury.

Headline: Kyle Monangai rushed eight times for 18 yards in the Bears’ Week 11 win over the Saints.
News Snippet: Monangai played for the first time since suffering a turf toe injury in Week 4, getting 17 snaps on the day. He had five less carries and nine less snaps than D’Andre Swift as Salvon Ahmed also got involved with six carries for 33 yards. Monangai’s first snap was to run a route on third-and-long on the Bears’ first possession while he started in the backfield on the second drive. The 24-year-old had no receptions and just one red zone carry on the day, though his snap share and touch split with Swift was at pre-injury levels. Fantasy managers should anticipate less Ahmed usage in future weeks; Monangai should be in the RB4 ranks for Week 12 against the Lions.

Headline: Greg Dulcich caught 2-of-7 targets for 12 yards in the Dolphins’ Week 11 loss to the Bills.
News Snippet: Dulcich saw the second-most targets on the team but ran a route on just 16 of the Dolphins’ 36 dropbacks. It’s nice to see Kyle McCord target him so often when he’s on the field, but Dulcich is not producing enough to be under consideration in fantasy leagues.

Headline: Joe Milton completed 11-of-21 attempts for 141 yards in the Eagles’ Week 11 win against the Steelers, adding five rushes for six yards.
News Snippet: Milton was in game manager mode as the Eagles maintained a lead throughout thanks to the team’s suffocating defense against Aaron Rodgers and the collapsing Steelers offense. Milton was not asked to do much, and he didn’t. He targeted DeVonta Smith — returning from a long injury absence — a team-high 12 times, missing him on a couple routine throws in the second half. Unless the Eagles face runaway negative game script, Milton won’t hold much fantasy value. He gets a good matchup next week against the Cowboys.

Headline: Chris Bell caught 1-of-4 targets for eight yards in the Dolphins’ Week 11 loss to the Bills.
News Snippet: Bell was questionable to return to the game after suffering a chest injury in the second quarter; however, he did return and ran 20 routes on 36 dropbacks, which was the third-most on the team. Bell still has a decent future given his pre-knee-injury upside, but it’s tough to roster him in redraft leagues right now.

Headline: Germie Bernard caught 6-of-10 targets for 40 yards in the Steelers’ Week 11 loss to the Eagles.
News Snippet: Bernard led the team in both pass routes and targets. He didn’t do much with his opportunity, which mostly included quick check-down passes from Aaron Rodgers. Roman Wilson returned from a finger injury and caught three balls for 43 yards while DK Metcalf was ejected for unsportsmanlike conduct in the third quarter. Max Hurleman, meanwhile, led the Steelers in receiving yards and caught the team’s lone touchdown while running just 15 routes. Bernard, who has 97 yards over his past four games, will be a deep league PPR option next week against the Broncos.

Headline: Malik Washington caught 3-of-6 targets for 30 yards in the Dolphins’ Week 11 loss to the Bills.
News Snippet: He also added two rushes for 11 yards. Washington made a tremendous one-handed catch on a fourth-down conversion late in the game, but there wasn’t much else happening for him on the day. His six targets were the third-most on the team, but he ran a route on 32 of the team’s 36 dropbacks, which was the most on the team. He’s a risky FLEX play against the Jets next week.

Headline: Dak Prescott completed 28-of-33 passes for 325 yards and four touchdowns in the Cowboys’ 51-30, Week 11 win over the Titans, adding four carries for nine yards and a fifth touchdown.
News Snippet: Prescott totaled 10 touchdowns from Weeks 4-9. He’s now matched that total over his past two starts, including nine scores through the air. Today he found “the usual” of CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens and Javonte Williams for scoring strikes while tacking on role player Brevyn Spann-Ford. Prescott’s score on the ground was a lunge for the pylon where he was initially, confusingly labeled out of bounds. He was not, and the Cowboys’ unstoppable offensive effort marched on. Playing his best football just in time for Thanksgiving, Prescott will have the opportunity to stay hot vs. a short-handed Eagles D. Things then get dicier for fantasy managers, with the Cowboys visiting Seattle in Week 13 before an unseasonably late Week 14 bye.

Headline: Sam LaPorta caught 3-of-6 targets for 62 yards in the Lions’ Week 11 win over the Bucs.
News Snippet: Coming off a month of quiet showings, this goes down as a rebound for LaPorta, even if it doesn’t do all that much for fantasy managers. LaPorta tied for a team-high in targets and trailed only Jameson Williams in yards. The only downside to his performance is that Brock Wright and Tyler Conklin combined for three catches and 60 yards. With a Thanksgiving shootout versus the Bears on tap, LaPorta will get one more game in the TE1 ranks for Week 12.

Headline: Caleb Douglas caught 2-of-10 targets for 30 yards in the Dolphins’ Week 11 loss to the Bills.
News Snippet: Douglas was the clear featured receiver in Miami’s offense this week, but it didn’t really amount to anything. On one possession, he was targeted on three straight passes in the end zone. He dropped one, was overthrown on one, and had the other broken up. He also had another drop on a pass inside Buffalo’s 20-yard line on the final drive of the game, but that wouldn’t have changed the outcome of the game at all. He should remain on the FLEX radar next week against the Jets.

Headline: Ollie Gordon II rushed 11 times for 69 yards in the Dolphins’ Week 11 loss to the Bills.
News Snippet: Gordon looked good in this one and consistently earned extra yards on his carries, but he simply didn’t get enough chances. Much of that is because Miami ran just 55 plays in this game and was trailing by two scores for almost the entire thing. Gordon should be in the RB2 conversation next weekend against the Jets.

Headline: Bhayshul Tuten exited the field in Week 11 against the Giants.
News Snippet: Tuten was dinged up on the first play of the game and was later seen riding the exercise bike on the sideline. He came into the game battling ankle and knee issues that limited him in practice this week. He may have aggravated the injuries. Chris Rodriguez would take over as the team’s lead back if Tuten misses time.

Headline: Jameson Williams caught all four of his targets for 93 yards and a touchdown in the Lions’ Week 11 win over the Bucs.
News Snippet: Williams busted his two-game slump with a 57-yard score in the third quarter. As he tends to do, Williams simply blew by the Bucs’ defense on a deep shot and saw nothing but grass in front of him. Despite the strong fantasy outing, Williams still finished fourth on the team in targets, behind all of the usual suspects. Williams has been one of the most frustrating fantasy options this year, but managers have to stick with him through the lulls to find spike weeks like today. He will be in the WR2 mix for a potential shootout with the Bears next week.

Headline: D’Andre Swift rushed 13 times for 51 yards and a fumble in the Bears’ Week 11 win over the Saints, adding two receptions for eight yards and a touchdown.
News Snippet: Swift got the first three touches of the game for the Bears, operating as the lead back with Kyle Monangai back. His snaps took a dip, especially after a fourth quarter fumble. A shovel pass from Caleb Williams for a receiving score in the first half saved his fantasy production as Bears drives stalled frequently against the Saints. The good news is that Swift is still the lead back, though Monangai’s return will eat into his workload. Swift belongs in the fantasy RB2 ranks for a Week 12 Thanksgiving matchup against the Lions.

Headline: Roman Wilson caught 3-of-6 targets for 43 yards in the Steelers’ Week 11 loss to the Eagles.
News Snippet: Returning from a finger injury, Wilson ran a route on 41 of the team’s 59 drop backs and was second to Max Hurleman in receptions and receiving yards. Aaron Rodgers nearly connected with the speedy Wilson on a long ball in the second half. Wilson’s playing time may have been affected by DK Metcalf’s second half ejection after repeated fights with Philadelphia defenders. Wilson will have some deep league value in the run-first Steelers offense, including next week against the Broncos.

Headline: Dawson Knox caught 2-of-3 targets for 31 yards in the Bills’ Week 11 win over the Dolphins.
News Snippet: Despite Dalton Kincaid not being active on Sunday, Knox was not a huge part of the passing game. He did run a route on 29 of 52 dropbacks, which was fourth-most on the team, but he simply wasn’t targeted much. Kincaid is expected to return on Thursday against the Chiefs, which keeps Knox off the fantasy radar.

Headline: Keon Coleman caught 2-of-4 targets for 17 yards in the Bills’ Week 11 win over the Dolphins.
News Snippet: Despite the return of Tyrell Shavers, who is a strong blocking receiver, Coleman ran a route on 45 of the team’s 52 dropbacks and played on 63 of 78 snaps. Both of those were a team-high. It didn’t result in fantasy success, but it seems like Coleman has evolved into the “dirty work” receiver in Buffalo who can move the chains with tough catches and pick up key blocks in the running game. He’s not a fantasy option next week against the Chiefs.

Headline: Simi Fehoko caught 1-of-5 targets for two yards and a touchdown in Arizona’s Week 11 loss to the Chiefs.
News Snippet: He added three carries for seven yards. The 2021 fifth-round pick has suddenly become important at work, playing 47-of-49 snaps, but that does not mean he needs to be rostered in all but the deepest leagues given how poorly this offense is running.

Headline: Trey McBride caught 9-of-14 targets for 54 yards in Arizona’s Week 11 loss to the Chiefs.
News Snippet: It sure does feel hard to find overall TE1 upside the past few weeks with Michael Wilson on the shelf. McBride was peppered with targets in the blowout loss but was mostly just an underneath option. His long gain went for just nine yards. McBride will remain a TE1 next week against the Commanders, but it’s fair to question the ceiling.

Headline: DJ Moore caught 8-of-10 targets for 91 yards and a touchdown in the Bills’ Week 11 win over the Dolphins.
News Snippet: There was a scary moment in the second quarter when Moore jumped to try and break up an interception and came down hard, hyperextending his knee. He went right into the locker room, and it seemed like he might be done for the day, but he came back out in time for the next drive. There’s a chance the Bills give him a lighter week of practice with the Chiefs coming up on Thursday, but Moore will need to be a big part of the game plan if Buffalo is going to win that game.

Headline: Caleb Williams completed 15-of-23 passes for 181 yards, two touchdowns, and an interception in the Bears’ 21-13, Week 11 win over the Saints.
News Snippet: The Bears offense had its usual explosiveness, but struggled to finish drives. Williams’ mobility was on full display, using his legs to buy time and find receivers while adding 13 rushing yards before a pair of end-of-game kneels. He lofted up a fourth down end zone target to Kalif Raymond that was broken up in the first quarter and threw an interception in the second quarter. The drives that did end in touchdowns for the Bears in the first half came on a Williams shovel pass to D’Andre Swift and a toss to Colston Loveland in the flat he ran in for the score. Williams had completions of over 10 yards to five different receivers as he continued to push the ball downfield. His high-risk, high-reward style of play lends it self to splash plays to boost fantasy production. Williams will be in the low-end QB1 ranks for a Thanksgiving day matchup against the Lions.

Headline: Harrison Wallace caught 4-of-7 targets for 57 yards in Arizona’s Week 11 loss to the Chiefs.
News Snippet: It was the 2026 UDFA’s third game in the pros. He played 29-of-49 snaps. Wallace caught Arizona’s longest gain of the day, a 25-yarder. We guess we have to take the idea that Wallace could move towards FLEX value seriously as they move on to the Commanders in Week 12, but it is hard to imagine much fantasy value coming out of this team for the rest of the year outside of Trey McBride.

Headline: Chuba Hubbard rushed 27 times for 120 yards and two touchdowns in the Panthers’ Week 11 win over the Ravens.
News Snippet: Hubbard didn’t see a target in this one, but he more than made up for his lack of targets with his efficiency on the ground. The 27-year-old back saw 15 of his 27 rush attempts go for four or more yards, and ripped off an 18-yard touchdown run in the second quarter for his first score of the day. He scored again in the third quarter on a one-yard touchdown run and added a two-point conversion, to the delight of his fantasy managers. Fellow running back Jonathon Brooks (groin) was close to suiting up in this one and could be back for Week 12 when the Panthers take on the Buccaneers on Monday Night Football. Despite Brooks’ impending return, Hubbard remains a must-start and will be in the RB1 conversation next week.

Headline: Jahmyr Gibbs rushed 23 times for 98 yards in the Lions’ Week 11 win over the Bucs, adding four catches for 20 yards.
News Snippet: The Lions did a good job bottling Gibbs up for three quarters, but you can only keep him out of the end zone for so long. Gibbs punched in a one-yard score late in the fourth quarter to functionally seal the game. After a quick turnover-on-downs from the Bucs, he put the final nail in the coffin with another goal line touchdown. Gibbs entered the game tied for the league lead in touchdowns from scrimmage at 13. Now Christian McCaffrey needs to find the end zone twice to keep pace. Still putting up gaudy numbers every week, Gibbs is the unquestioned RB1 overall for his Week 12 game against the Bears.

Headline: Khalil Shakir caught 5-of-9 targets for 101 yards in the Bills’ Week 11 win over the Dolphins.
News Snippet: Shakir led the team in receiving yards and was second on the team in targets. He hauled in a 38-yard reception and a 32-yard reception, which fueled his day. One of those was on a long catch-and-run, and the other was on a broken play where Josh Allen was rolling out of the pocket and found Shakir. The 26-year-old receiver has a knack for getting open in space and will always be a big producer for Buffalo when they play defenses that like to play a lot of zone.

Headline: Aaron Rodgers completed 30-of-44 attempts for 227 yards and one touchdown in the Steelers’ Week 11 loss to the Eagles, adding five rushes for 29 yards.
News Snippet: Rodgers, as he has been for most of the season, was wildly inefficient against the Eagles. He posted a -4.1 EPA, barely better than Joe Milton. Rodgers again was in check-down mode, only trying a couple deep shots and holding the ball time and again. Rodgers took five sacks and narrowly avoided a handful of others as the Steelers offensive line was overwhelmed for the second straight week. Coming into Week 11, only Daniel Jones and Baker Mayfield had lower drop backs EPAs than Rodgers. He’ll be a superflex option in Week 12 against the Broncos.

Headline: Derrick Henry rushed 13 times for 94 yards and a touchdown in the Ravens’ Week 11 loss to the Panthers, adding four receptions for 17 additional yards.
News Snippet: Henry made the most of a plus matchup against a porous Panthers rush defense. The Big Dog’s 94 rushing yards were his most in any game since Week 5 against the Falcons, and he found the end zone on a 15-yard rushing touchdown in the fourth quarter to put the Ravens up 33-32. Unfortunately, Henry landed hard on his head on the play and had to be taken to the locker room to be evaluated for a concussion. While he didn’t return to the field, it was reported after the game that he cleared concussion protocol, meaning he should be in good shape to take on the Texans in Week 12. He will remain in the mix as a fringe RB1/RB2 for next week.

Headline: Jacoby Brissett completed 24-of-37 passes for 276 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in the Ravens’ 35-33, Week 11 loss to the Panthers.
News Snippet: It was another up-and-down performance for Brissett, who missed a handful of easy throws, but also made the most of a Declan Doyle trick play call in the first quarter. On the play, Derrick Henry took the snap from the wildcat formation and immediately handed it off to Justice Hill, who pitched it back to Brissett on what looked like a flea-flicker off an end-around run. After taking the toss from Hill, Brissett immediately found Rashod Bateman downfield for a 52-yard touchdown pass. It would be the only touchdown Brissett would throw on the day, although he did lead the Ravens on two touchdown-scoring drives, one of which came on the heels of a 34-yard pass to Devontez Walker. Despite some decent moments, a late interception in the fourth quarter, as the Ravens were looking to get in range for a game-winning field goal, will be what fans remember most, as the Ravens have now lost six straight after getting off to a strong 4-1 start. Brissett will be on the QB2 radar next week when the Ravens visit the Texans in a battle between two teams who have underperformed expectations this season.

Headline: Tyler Allgeier rushed seven times for 23 yards in Arizona’s Week 11 loss to the Chiefs.
News Snippet: He out-snapped Bam Knight 26-23 in a committee that has managed to keep even a slim amount of fantasy value from coming to fruition. Allgeier has 259 rushing yards on the season if you exclude the week they played the Dallas Cowboys.

Headline: Ty Johnson caught 7-of-8 targets for 55 yards in the Bills’ Week 11 win over the Dolphins.
News Snippet: Despite his status as a running back, Johnson’s value to the Bills is as a receiver and pass blocker. He was a crucial option for Josh Allen when under pressure today, and Johnson consistently makes one or two big receptions in the screen game each week. His eight targets were third on the team this week, as were his 55 yards rushing. Still, it would be Ray Davis who would get a lot of rushing value if James Cook were ever to get hurt, which limits Johnson’s appeal as a stash option.

Headline: DeVonta Smith caught 5-of-12 targets for 41 yards in the Eagles’ Week 11 win against the Steelers.
News Snippet: Returning from a two-month hamstring injury, Smith led the Eagles with a 57 percent target share. No other Eagles pass catcher saw more than five targets. Joe Milton missed a couple easy completions to Smith, one of which would have led to a chunk gain. It was a tough run-out for Smith, who looked fully healthy. Smith will be a solid option next week against a terrible Dallas secondary that was carved up by Cam Ward in Week 11.

Headline: James Cook rushed 22 times for 89 yards and a touchdown in the Bills’ Week 11 win over the Dolphins.
News Snippet: With this effort, Cook has set an NFL record with nine consecutive games with 75+ rushing yards and a touchdown. Only two other players in NFL history had done it for eight games in a row. It’s the perfect encapsulation of Cook’s fantasy value on this Buffalo offense. The presence of Josh Allen will limit the number of touchdowns and ceiling games Cook puts together, but he remains one of the most consistent producers at the running back position in fantasy football. He remains an RB1, even in a tough matchup against the Chiefs.

Headline: Tyler Shough completed 25-of-42 attempts for 222 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in the Saints’ 21-13 Week 11 loss to the Bears, adding three rushes for 34 yards.
News Snippet: Shough and the Saints offense got off to another slow start. After a scoreless first quarter, Shough threw an interception in New Orleans territory in the second quarter. He was able to later connect with Alvin Kamara for a fourth-and-goal touchdown pass while a 30-yard scramble in the two minute drill led to a Saints field goal at the end of the half. The second half saw little offense from the Saints as they scored just one field goal the rest of the game. Shough failed to connect with Noah Fant on a crucial red zone fourth down and took a 13-yard sack in the two-minute drill at the end of the game. He averaged 5.3 yards per attempt in another inefficient showing. Shough belongs in the fantasy QB2 ranks for a Week 12 matchup against the Bengals.

Headline: Bryce Young completed 22-of-30 passes for 254 yards, two touchdowns, and one interception in the Panthers’ 35-33, Week 11 win over the Ravens.
News Snippet: Young and the Panthers had a much-needed bounce-back performance in Sunday’s win over the Ravens. After struggling to move the ball in Week 10’s win over the Saints, Young and the Panthers overcame an early safety on their opening drive to string together a nice five-play, 79-yard drive in the first quarter that included a 35-yard completion to Jalen Coker, which was followed by a 23-yard touchdown pass to tight end Mitchell Evans. In the second quarter, Young connected with Tetairoa McMillan for a seven-yard touchdown pass in the end zone to put the Panthers up 22-19 after Chuba Hubbard ran in a two-point conversion. Young’s lone interception came on another end zone target to McMillan in the third quarter, but the mistake didn’t prove too costly, as the Ravens went three-and-out on the ensuing drive. Young took back-to-back sacks to start a drive in the fourth quarter after the Panthers’ defense forced a turnover of their own, spoiling a chance to go up by two possessions, but the Panthers’ defense held up its end of the bargain late when it forced an interception of Jacoby Brissett to end any hopes of a comeback attempt. With all 32 teams playing in Week 12, Young will be on the mid-to-high-end QB2 radar next week against the Buccaneers.

Headline: Bam Knight rushed seven times for 35 yards in Arizona’s Week 11 loss to the Chiefs, adding a catch on his only target for 10 yards.
News Snippet: Knight had three touches for three yards at halftime, but turned in a half-reasonable FLEX line once the Cardinals started running clock in the fourth quarter. He had 23 snaps to Tyler Allgeier’s 26. Even against the Commanders, this feels like a tough click in Week 12.

Headline: Brock Bowers (ankle/quad) is inactive for Week 11 against the Broncos.
News Snippet: Bowers wasn’t spotted on the field during warmups, so he may not have been that close to playing today after all. He’s now eyeing a Week 12 return against the Browns. Michael Mayer will pick up a few extra targets versus Denver, putting him on the TE1/2 border. Also inactive for the Raiders are WR Dont’e Thornton Jr., WR Malik Benson, S Tristin McCollum, S Dalton Johnson, OG Bryce Cabeldue, and DT Tonka Hemingway.

Headline: The Jets declared Omar Cooper Jr., CB Jarvis Brownlee Jr., WR Isaiah Williams, LB Trevin Wallace, TE Jelani Woods and ED Nate Lynn inactive for Week 11 against the Chargers.
News Snippet: Removing Cooper and Williams leaves Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell as the team’s top two wide receivers. Kenyon Sadiq and Mason Taylor could benefit as well. Geno Smith will play through his ankle injury today, after beginning the week in the questionable column. A run-heavy, quick-passing game plan could be incoming, given Smith’s ailment.

Headline: Chris Bell is questionable to return to Week 11 against the Bills with a chest injury.
News Snippet: Bell and Bills safety Damar Hamlin collided on a Hamlin interception in the second quarter. It seemed like Bell and Hamlin slammed their helmets into one another, but Bell’s injury designation says chest. It’s been a season of tough injury luck for Bell, who has battled a knee injury all season after having offseason surgery.

Headline: Charlie Kolar (concussion) is active for Week 11 against the Jets.
News Snippet: Kolar, David Njoku and Oronde Gadsden will form a three-player committee this afternoon. None of them warrant TE1 treatment, though they provide Justin Herbert with safety-blanket options and should help out in the run game.

Headline: Ladd McConkey (back) is active for Week 11 against the Jets.
News Snippet: McConkey’s injuries have made him difficult to trust this season, but the Chargers have funneled targets his way when active. He should be viewed as a WR3 with volume-based upside, now evidently healthy enough to play. The Chargers declared LB Daiyan Henley, CB Tarheeb Still, WR Brenen Thompson, S Kendall Williamson, G Alex Harkey and WR KeAndre Lambert-Smith inactive for Week 11 against the Jets.

Headline: Roschon Johnson suffered an ankle injury in the Bears’ Week 11 game against the Saints and is doubtful to return.
News Snippet: Johnson was carted to the locker room in the first quarter against the Saints. He was announced to have an ankle injury and is doubtful to return. With Kyle Monangai back, the Bears had depth in the backfield again but lose a special teamer and third-string running back in Johnson against the Saints.

Headline: Lions declared CB D.J. Reed, CB Ennis Rakestraw Jr., DB Ketih Abney II, LB Amen Ogbongbemiga, EDGE Tyrus Wheat, and DL Mekhi Wingo inactive for Week 11 against the Bucs.
News Snippet: Reed made seven starts this year before injuring his hip a few weeks ago. Rakestraw has been a depth option so far, but that would have been useful to have around with Reed out. The Lions’ defense will be as vulnerable as ever this week, though it’s anyone’s guess as to whether a hobbled Baker Mayfield will take advantage.

Headline: Dolphins declared S Dante Trader Jr., CB Jaylin Simpson, P Bradley Pinion, OL Christian Haynes, OL Caedan Wallace, TE Justin Joly, and WR Jared Wayne inactive for Week 11 against the Bills.
News Snippet: Trader Jr. is the Dolphins’ starting strong safety, but the rest of the inactives are depth pieces. Simpson does see the field as a backup cornerback, so the Dolphins will be down two members of the secondary in a game against Josh Allen, which is never great news.

Headline: Tyrell Shavers (knee) is active and will make his season debut in Week 11 against the Dolphins.
News Snippet: Shavers has been sidelined all season after tearing his ACL in a playoff win over Jacksonville last year. The 27-year-old had emerged as the team’s best blocking wide receiver last year and had seen his snap count increase as the season went on. He’s unlikely to be a fantasy factor, but it would not be surprising to see him play a decent amount of snaps once he is fully ramped up because of the value he provides in the running game. This means rookie Skyler Bell is back to being a game-day inactive.

Headline: Dalton Kincaid is inactive for Week 11 against the Dolphins.
News Snippet: Kincaid was listed as questionable with (thumb/ankle) injuries, but he will not suit up. This makes sense as a cautionary move for the Bills, who already ruled out starting cornerback Christian Benford and starting linebacker Dorian Williams. The Bills are nearly a 17-point favorite against the Dolphins on Sunday and then will face the Chiefs on Thursday night. Except Dawson Knox to be more involved in this game in Week 11, but we wouldn’t be surprised if the Bills are running the ball a lot in the second half. The Bills’ full inactives are: WR Skyler Bell, TE Dalton Kincaid, OT Jude Bowry, DL T.J. Sanders, ILB Dorian Williams, OLB Mike Danna, and CB Christian Benford.

Headline: Roman Wilson (finger) is active for Week 11 against the Eagles.
News Snippet: Wilson, who accounted for 16 percent of the Steelers’ targets and 39 percent of the team’s air yards before sustaining a finger injury in Week 5, will make his return to the lineup and likely make Germie Bernard all but unplayable in 12-team leagues. Wilson can be slotted in as a high-variance flex or second flex against the Eagles. The Steelers declared WR Kaden Wetjen, QBs Drew Allar Will Howard, Sean Murphy-Bunting, RB Eli Heidenreich, OLB Nick Herbig, and DL Gabe Rubio inactive.

Headline: Chiefs declared RB Kenneth Walker (groin) inactive for Kansas City’s Week 11 game against the Cardinals.
News Snippet: It’s Emmett Johnson szn once more. Also inactive for the Chiefs are QB Garrett Nussmeier (third quarterback), OL Jaylon Moore (ankle), OL Trey Smith (concussion), DT Omarr Norman-Lott (knee), DT Peter Woods (neck) and CB Melvin Smith. Norman-Lott and Woods were both questionable and will not play. The others were ruled out on Friday.

Headline: Saints declared LB Pete Werner, CB Martin Emerson Jr., RB Audric Estime, OT Asim Richards, OT Taliese Fuaga, C Erik McCoy, and QB Zach Wilson inactive for Week 11 against the Bears.
News Snippet: Estime was seeing nearly half of the Saints’ backfield snaps up to last week. With Travis Etienne ramping back up from injury, the Saints choose to deactivate Estime, keeping Etienne as the primary back, Alvin Kamara as the pass-catching back, and rookie CJ Donaldson as the third-string in what has been a frustrating committee for fantasy purposes. Zach Wilson is the emergency third quarterback while Werner (hamstring), Emerson (concussion), Richards (knee), Fuaga (knee), and McCoy (biceps) are all out with injury, leaving the offensive line and defense short-handed against the Bears.

Headline: Titans declared RB Nicholas Singleton, LB Mohamoud Diabate, CB Jaylon Jones, DT Jackie Marshall and OT Brandon Crenshaw-Dickson inactive for Week 11 against the Cowboys.
News Snippet: With Tyjae Spears on injured reserve, it’s a poor sign for fifth-round rookie Singleton that he is still getting healthy scratched in Week 11.

Headline: Darren Waller (knee) is active for the Panthers’ Week 11 against the Ravens.
News Snippet: Waller was questionable with a knee injury entering the weekend, but will be good to go in what is somewhat of a revenge game against the team that drafted him in the sixth round back in 2015. The 34-year old tight end profiles as a boom-or-bust TE2 against a Ravens defense that has allowed the 10th-most PPR points per game (14.1) to opposing tight ends over its last five games. In addition to Waller, fellow tight end Tommy Tremble (knee) is also active, while TE Ja’Tavion Sanders, QB Haynes King, RB AJ Dillon, LB Bobby Okereke, C Sam Hecht, and DT TeRah Edwards will all be inactive for this one.

Headline: Cardinals declared QB Carson Beck, CB Starling Thomas V, OL Kingsley Eguakun, OL Jon Gaines (ankle) and DL Andrew Billings inactive for Arizona’s Week 11 game against the Chiefs.
News Snippet: Just in case you were off the grid Saturday: Josh Johnson will start for the Cardinals against the Chiefs, becoming the fourth quarterback in four weeks for a team critics are calling “one of mankind’s most awful crimes.” OK, not really, but they are 15.5-point dogs. Johnson is probably one of the three worst superflex quarterbacks to have to start this week on a short slate.

Headline: Cowboys declared TE Jake Ferguson, OG Tyler Booker, S P.J. Locke, WR Jonathan Mingo, LB Jaishawn Barham and DT Jonathan Bullard inactive for Week 11 against the Titans.
News Snippet: Ferguson has barely played since Week 7. Although he is merely week to week with his ankle and knee issues, the formerly fantasy relevant seam stretcher seems unlikely to be a 12-team league factor down the stretch.

Headline: DeVonta Smith (hamstring) is active for Week 11 against the Steelers.
News Snippet: Smith will finally make his return to game action after a two-month hamstring injury. Before the injury, he had accounted for 30 percent of the team’s targets and 47 percent of the team’s air yards. Smith’s 40 percent first-read target share was among the highest in the NFL over the season’s first month. He should be a decent WR3 here with Joe Milton under center. Eagles declared QB Cole Payton, CB Mac McWilliams, LB Smael Mondon Jr., LB Ajani Cornelius, and OL Jake Majors inactive against the Steelers.

Headline: Sione Vaki (ankle) is active for Week 11 against the Bucs.
News Snippet: Vaki will continue to back up Jahmyr Gibbs, though that role hasn’t produced much fantasy value this year. He will only see a meaningful amount of touches if the Lions blow out the Bucs, which could happen. Vaki is buried in the RB5 ranks for now.

Headline: Bears declared QB Case Keenum, OL Jordan McFadden, CB Kyler Gordon, DL Jayden Loving, and LB Keyshaun Elliott inactive for Week 11 against the Saints.
