News Snippet: Gordon was already declared out with a shoulder injury heading into the weekend. Rookie wide receiver Zavion Thomas (ankle) entered the day questionable, but will be active after missing Friday’s practice. Case Keenum will be the team’s emergency third quarterback.

Headline: Ravens declared CB Marlon Humphrey, FS Jaylinn Hawkins, RB Adam Randall, OG Emery Jones, DT Nnamdi Madubuike, and QB Kedon Slovis inactive for Week 11 against the Panthers.
News Snippet: Humphrey, Madubuike, and Hawkins were all ruled out before the weekend. The Ravens will look to end a five-game skid in Jacoby Brissett’s second start with the team and face a Panthers defense that is near the bottom of the league at stopping the run, which could bode well for Derrick Henry and a ground game that has been stagnant in recent weeks.

Headline: Baker Mayfield (foot) is active for Week 11 against the Lions.
News Snippet: Mayfield is going to try to play through the plantar fascia injury he suffered in Week 9 before the Bucs’ bye. Expect the Bucs to lean on their ground game for as long as possible to protect Mayfield. Even in a good matchup, it’s hard to treat him as anything better than a mid-range QB2. EDGE Yaya Diaby is also active. Inactive for the Bucs are DT DeMonte Capehart, CB Ayden Garnes, OG Trevor Keegan, OG Billy Schrauth, QB Easton Stick, and S Antoine Winfield Jr.

Headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports there is “not a lot of optimism” that Brock Bowers (ankle/quad) will play in Week 11 against the Broncos.
News Snippet: Bowers returned to practice earlier in the week and was listed as questionable on Friday. Schefter noted that Bowers is pushing to play, but we doubt the team will let him suit up after suffering another ankle injury. That’s on top of the quad issue, which seems to be minor compared to the ankle. Assuming Bowers is out, Michael Mayer should see an uptick in targets against a Denver defense that has bled fantasy points to tight ends this season. He would be a solid streaming option if Bowers is ruled out.

Headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Drake Maye (fractured fibula) is expected to miss at least six weeks.
News Snippet: A six-week absence would technically allow Maye to return late in the regular season, but Rapoport then followed up by saying he has an “outside chance” at playing if the Pats make the playoffs. We suspect the Patriots would, at most, use the final weeks of the regular season to get Maye back on the practice field. Tommy DeVito is currently their starting quarterback and they’re sitting at 5-5, so a playoff berth doesn’t appear to be in the cards. Rapoport also mentioned Daniel Jones as an option in Maye’s absence. We doubt he saves New England’s season, but he would be an upgrade over DeVito.

Headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports the Ravens offered the Colts a fourth-round pick for Daniel Jones and a conditional fifth-round pick.
News Snippet: The fifth-round pick returned to the Colts if the Ravens made the playoffs. At worst, the Colts would have upgraded one of their Day Three picks. At best, they could have walked away with an extra fourth-round selection. They weren’t getting a king’s ransom for Jones, but it’s better than what they walked away with two weeks later when they cut him. The Colts’ mismanagement of the Jones situation will go down as a true blunder by a front office in disarray. Jones could still wind up in Baltimore as a free agent, assuming he clears waivers later this week.

Headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Davante Adams sounds like a “long shot” to play in Week 13 against the Chiefs.
News Snippet: Adams isn’t expected to play in Week 12. The Rams get the Packers on Wednesday before Thanksgiving, and the tight turnaround makes a Week 12 return all but impossible. Head coach Sean McVay said Week 13 against Kansas City was a “possibility” earlier this week. That sounds unlikely now as well. Rapoport said Adams is eyeing a mid-December return. With Puka Nacua done for the year, the Rams are down to Konata Mumpfield and Tutu Atwell as their top wide receivers for at least a few more weeks.

Headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Micah Parsons is “on track” to play in Week 12 against the Rams.
News Snippet: This isn’t a major surprise as head coach Matt LaFleur told reporters on Monday that he was hopeful Parsons would play in Week 12. It sounds like that timeline remains in the cards. Parsons has missed the first three months of the season while recovering from a torn ACL and meniscus injuries he suffered late last year. Getting Parsons back will be a huge boost for a Packers defense that hasn’t done much this year. Parsons had 12.5 sacks in 14 games with the Packers last year.

Headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter believes Daniel Jones will “draw interest” from the Patriots and Ravens.
News Snippet: Schefter didn’t directly cite his sources on this, so he may just be connecting dots. Still, the two teams make loads of sense for the downtrodden quarterback. The Patriots are expected to be without Drake Maye for at least the rest of the regular season. At 5-5, they’re still in the hunt for a Wild Card bid, though their odds of making the postseason will all but disappear if Tommy DeVito remains their starting quarterback. The Ravens are in a similar spot, though they’ve already addressed the quarterback position via Jacoby Brissett. Schefter notes that the most likely outcome is that Jones waits for a more attractive spot to open up. He is expected to clear waivers later this week, at which point he will become an unrestricted free agent.

Headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports the Colts are shutting down Alec Pierce (heel) for the remainder of the 2026 season.
News Snippet: Pierce signed a four-year, $114 million contract in the offseason. He almost immediately underwent surgery and was expected to miss three months, though it took a bit longer than that. There was also a mix-up about whether or not he underwent a second PRP injection, which at-the-time GM Chris Ballard denied. He was sidelined for a bit longer than that but did play in Week 1. Pierce then re-injured his heel in Week 2, functionally ending his season. The team has now chosen to shut him down to avoid any chance of further complications. It sounds like he will be good to go for 2027. Pierce’s season ends with five catches for 72 scoreless yards. He will return to a rebuilding Colts roster that is unlikely to support his WR3 fantasy case next year.

Headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Baker Mayfield (foot) will play in Week 11 against the Lions.
News Snippet: Mayfield looked unlikely to play after missing Wednesday’s practice. He inexplicably returned for Thursday’s session before being listed as questionable the next day. He’s dealing with a plantar fascia injury that hobbled him in the team’s Week 9 loss to the Bears. A Week 10 bye was just enough time off to get him back on the field without any time missed. Even in a great matchup with the Lions, it’s hard to trust Mayfield as anything other than a mid-range QB2.

Headline: Mike Evans (Achilles) will play in Week 11 against the Vikings.
News Snippet: Evans’ agent posted a video on his Instagram that can only be described as the corniest thing you will see today. In it, he vaguely announced that Evans was back after missing a few weeks with Achilles tendinitis. Evans will likely be managing this injury for the rest of the season, so we wouldn’t be surprised if he returns on a bit of a pitch count. Still, Evans was operating as the team’s unquestioned WR1 before suffering the injury. He will be on the WR2/3 border for his first game back.

Headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Puka Nacua (MCL surgery) will be sidelined 4-5 months.
News Snippet: This confirms Nacua will not only miss the remainder of the regular season, but would be unavailable for any potential Super Bowl run for the pre-season favorites. Schefter did add that Nacua’s knee “checked out clean aside from the MCL.” That’s good news heading into Nacua’s potential free agency, though he is nevertheless at a low ebb in his up-and-down Rams tenure. The ups have been any time Nacua takes the field. The downs have been how often he has been sidelined, as well as his off-the-field issues. Going on 26, Nacua would make a lot of sense as a franchise tag candidate, or perhaps a tag-and-trade for the Rams.

Headline: Panthers ruled out Jonathon Brooks (groin) for Week 11 against the Ravens.
News Snippet: Brooks will miss his seventh consecutive game in Week 11, leaving Chuba Hubbard to a true workhorse role for another week. The matchup is less than ideal against the Ravens but fantasy managers can continue riding the bump in volume to a high end RB2 profile for the veteran back.

Headline: Kyren Williams (toe) was limited Saturday but is expected to play in Week 12 against the Packers.
News Snippet: Williams is reportedly dealing with “soreness” in his toe and was limited in practice Saturday as a result. ESPN’s Sarah Barshop added that Williams is expected to play on Wednesday against the Packers. Expect him to continue working in a strict timeshare with Blake Corum coming out of the team’s Week 11 bye.

Headline: Andrei Iosivas (thumb) is doubtful for Week 11 against the Commanders.
News Snippet: Iosivas was practicing in full throughout the week, making his designation somewhat puzzling as he attempts to return from injured reserve. The team will have another week to activate the young wide receiver before he will be forced to remain on injured reserve for the remainder of the season.

Headline: Eagles placed WR Dontayvion Wicks (ankle/foot) on injured reserve.
News Snippet: Wicks has already missed the previous three games with an ankle injury and now finds himself sent to injured reserve, meaning he will miss at least seven games total with poorly timed injuries. He saw a “foot” designation added to his status during a week of limited showings, which is presumably the issue that lands him on injured reserve. DeVonta Smith, who returns from an extended absence this week, Makai Lemon, and Darius Cooper are likely to hold down the starting wide receiver positions in Wicks’ absence.

Headline: Treylon Burks (foot) was removed from the injury report Saturday and will play in Week 11 against the Bengals.
News Snippet: Burks surprisingly went from a full session Thursday and a no-show Friday, prompting uncertainty regarding his expected availability for Monday Night Football against the Bengals. He quickly put those worries to rest with a full practice Saturday and was removed from the injury report. Expect Burks to continue operating in a featured role on the perimeter in the absence of Terry McLaurin.

Headline: Rachaad White (heel) is questionable for Week 11 against the Bengals.
News Snippet: White’s week of practice was troubling, first appearing on the injury report on Friday with a limited designation due to a heel ailment before being downgraded to a “DNP” Saturday. Even so, head coach Dan Quinn indicated the veteran back is “on track” for Monday Night Football. Assuming he is active, White is likely to slot back into the primary change of pace role behind Jacory Croskey-Merritt, the latter of whom appears set to be activated from injured reserve in time for Monday.

Headline: Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) is questionable for Week 11 against the Bengals.
News Snippet: Croskey-Merritt managed a week of full practices as he attempts to return from injured reserve, and while the team has not yet activated him, he appears to be trending in the right direction for his first game action since Week 5. Rachaad White, also listed as questionable, would likely shift back to a primary change of pace role, should Croskey-Merritt return.

Headline: Steelers did not activate Michael Pittman (foot) ahead of Week 11.
News Snippet: Pittman will remain on injured reserve for at least another week. The team gets back fellow wide receiver Roman Wilson, who should join DK Metcalf and rookie Germie Bernard as the starters from 11-personnel. Fantasy managers are likely only able to confidently start Metcalf against the Eagles.

Headline: Steelers activated WR Roman Wilson (hand) from injured reserve.
News Snippet: Wilson ended up staying on injured reserve for the minimum four games as he dealt with a hand injury, returning to a roster approaching full health, although fellow wide receiver Michael Pittman was not activated from injured reserve ahead of Week 11.Fantasy managers are likely only able to confidently start Metcalf against the Eagles on Sunday.

Headline: Cardinals ruled out Carson Beck (back) for Week 11 against the Chiefs.
News Snippet: That paves the way for 36-year-old journeyman quarterback Josh Johnson to draw the start under center for the Cardinals after being added to the team less than two weeks ago. Dynasty managers will be forced to wait longer for the first extended look at the third-round rookie as the Cardinals continue forward with insurmountable injuries up and down their roster in what has quickly become a lost season. Downgrade the primary skill position players in a difficult matchup against the Chiefs in Week 11.

Headline: Titans placed RB Tyjae Spears (knee) on injured reserve.
News Snippet: Spears will now miss the next four games, at minimum, as he tends to a knee injury that has plagued him in recent weeks. Spears previously missed two games in Week 7 and Week 8 before returning to a modest workload in Week 9 after the team’s bye. Tony Pollard should continue operating in a true workhorse role and gets one of the top matchups in the league against the Cowboys in Week 11. Fantasy managers can continue to treat Pollard as a volume-driven RB1 after a slow start to the season.

Headline: Commanders HC Dan Quinn told reporters RB Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) is “trending the right way” ahead of the matchup with the Bengals in Week 11.
News Snippet: Quinn said Croskey-Merritt had a great week and is trending the right way for Monday’s game against the Bengals. It’s great news for fantasy managers and the Commanders as backup running back Rachaad White (heel) missed practice Saturday. Croskey-Merritt deserves FLEX consideration assuming he’s active against the Bengals this week.

Headline: Rachaad White (heel) missed practice on Saturday.
News Snippet: White was added to the injury report and was a limited participant in practice on Friday. His missed practice Saturday is another bad sign for the 27-year-old running back’s availability. With Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) trending towards being available, White doesn’t seem to have much fantasy value at the moment. CB Amik Robertson, who was seen limping in the locker room on Friday, also missed practice Saturday.

Headline: CBS Sports’ Matt Zenitz reports Titans WR Carnell Tate (shoulder) is likely to return against the Cowboys in Week 11.
News Snippet: Tate hasn’t played since Week 7 due to a shoulder injury. Still officially questionable, Zenitz reports Tate is likely to play in Week 11. While he’s been out for over a month, Tate got in a full practice on Friday. He’ll be a high-end WR3 in a plus matchup against the brutal Cowboys defense.

Headline: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports Buccaneers QB Baker Mayfield (foot) is dealing with a plantar fascia injury.
News Snippet: While Mayfield remains on track to play against the Lions on Sunday, he’s dealing with a painful plantar fascia injury, according to Pelissero. If the 31-year-old gunslinger suits up in Week 11, he’ll wear a special orthotic and new cleats to help stabilize his foot. Mayfield looked doubtful to play earlier in the week and even missed practice Wednesday before getting in a pair of limited sessions. Jalon Daniels would start if Mayfield isn’t able to play this week.

Headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler described Rams WR Puka Nacua’s future with the team as “very uncertain.”
News Snippet: Nothing earth-shattering here from Fowler. Appearing on ESPN’s SportsCenter Saturday morning, the NFL Insider noted that Nacua is dealing with a significant MCL injury and a three-game suspension from the NFL. With Nacua unlikely to return this season, Fowler says this isn’t the kind of momentum the 25-year-old receiver wanted heading into free agency, where he’ll be the best player available. The Rams can extend him, franchise tag him or let him hit the open market this offseason. As Fowler says, it’s something the Rams have to sort out.

Headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports that Mike Evans (Achilles) “is trending in the right direction” for Week 11 against the Vikings.
News Snippet: Rapoport does note, however, that Evans is “a little sore” after returning to practice on Thursday. The 49ers will make a decision on Evans’ Week 11 status on Saturday. If active, Evans will carry some re-injury risk, but reports have consistently indicated that the 49ers learned a lot from Christian McCaffrey’s bilateral Achilles tendinitis in 2024. It seems safe to assume that if Evans is active, his Achilles tendon is in good shape. Evans may not immediately return to his pre-injury form against the Vikings’ elite defense, but he should be in fantasy football lineups.

Headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports that Puka Nacua’s (knee/toe) recovery timeline “does not match up” with a potential return for Super Bowl LXI.
News Snippet: Nacua is currently on injured reserve, recovering from MCL and PCL sprains, along with a turf toe injury. He will also serve a three-game suspension on injured reserve, following the Rams’ Week 11 bye. The superstar wide receiver underwent surgery to repair his MCL on Tuesday, and Rapoport believes we have “almost certainly” seen the last of Nacua in the 2026 season. He is set to enter free agency this offseason, and it is unclear whether the Rams will extend him, franchise tag him or allow him to walk.

Headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport believes the Patriots and Ravens are “potential landing spots” for Daniel Jones.
News Snippet: Jones seemingly has decent odds of passing through waivers unclaimed, but he would be free to sign with any team after that. Rapoport adds that Jones is “still working his way back” from last year’s Achilles tendon rupture in his right, plant leg. Jones had a $10 million injury guarantee in his contract that is said to have been a factor in his release. Were he to sign with the Patriots, he could compete for the starting role with Tommy DeVito. Jacoby Brissett would probably be able to fend him off initially, were he to land in New England.

Headline: Team reporter Darren Urban believes Josh Johnson will “probably” start in Week 11 against the Cardinals.
News Snippet: Rookie Carson Beck is dealing with back spasms again, so recently signed journeyman Johnson will likely get the start this week. Urban notes that Johnson “played significant snaps for LaFleur in two games for the Jets in 2021, " completing 55-for-81 passes for 621 yards, five touchdowns and two interceptions. With six teams on bye, Johnson, 40, is in the low-end QB2 conversation.

Headline: Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) is not on the Broncos’ final injury report and will play in Week 11 against the Raiders.
News Snippet: Hufanga has not played since Week 5. He nearly returned in Week 9, pre-bye, but was unable to do so. His return could be helpful for a Broncos’ defense that struggles to cover tight ends. Broncos S Brandon Jones (hamstring) is questionable to play, and CB Riley Moss (concussion) is good to go.

Headline: Charlie Kolar (concussion) is questionable for Los Angeles’ Week 11 game against the Jets.
News Snippet: Kolar had not practiced either of the first two days of the week before this sudden Friday revival where he got in a limited session. We’d be surprised if he ultimately played coming off a short week, but no Chargers tight end is ultimately compelling with or without Kolar in the lineup.

Headline: Ladd McConkey (back) is questionable for Los Angeles’ Week 11 game against the Jets.
News Snippet: McConkey was limited in all three sessions this week and was a shadow docket rule out in Week 9 while being a straight inactive in Week 10. Actually practicing ahead of this game is a sign things are better, but he’ll be no more than a WR3 in this dilapidated passing attack between the re-injury risk and the lack of upside. Yes, even against the Jets.

Headline: Isaiah Likely (groin) is not on the Giants’ final injury report and will play in Week 11 against the Jaguars.
News Snippet: Likely sat out on Friday after practicing in full, injury-free, on Wednesday and Thursday. With six teams on bye and very few reliable tight end options in fantasy, Likely remains in the TE1 tier. Monitoring his status throughout the weekend will be worthwhile. Hopefully, we continue to get positive reports on his groin injury. Likely notably dealt with a groin injury back in Week 5.

Headline: Matt Gay (hip) is questionable for Las Vegas’ Week 11 game against the Broncos.
News Snippet: Kansei Matsuzawa is on the Raiders’ practice squad and would presumably be elevated if the team rules out Gay. Neither player seems especially likely to be a good fantasy bet this week against the Broncos with a rookie quarterback under center.

Headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Ladd McConkey (back) is expected to play in Week 11 against the Jets.
News Snippet: McConkey experienced back spasms in pre-game warmups two weeks ago. The Chargers didn’t announce that until the game had started and he did not play a snap. The team had the courtesy to rule him out ahead of kickoff last week. He got in three limited sessions this week before being listed as questionable. McConkey has been the Chargers’ most effective wideout when healthy, but that has been an exceedingly rare occurrence this year. We suspect he’s still not at full strength. With the risk of a re-injury looming, fantasy managers should treat him as a WR3, even if his ceiling his much higher.

Headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports that Bud Dupree has requested his release from the Chargers.
News Snippet: Fowler also reveals that Dupree asked to be released in the offseason, but the Chargers have been unwilling to grant it. Dupree is playing infrequently and has just two quarterback pressures and one tackle. Releasing him would reduce their depth, but he is not a critical defender for this 1-8 squad. Stay tuned.

Headline: Chris Rodriguez is not on Jacksonville’s final Week 11 injury report.
News Snippet: With Bhayshul Tuten not on the report either, Rodriguez looks likely to reprise his role as a clear backup against the Giants. He will not be worth gambling on in the FLEX spot without dramatic Tuten news ahead of Sunday.

Headline: Rachaad White (heel) was added to the injury report as a limited participant on Friday.
News Snippet: Mid-week additions to the injury report are generally a bad sign for a player’s availability. Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) is also practicing in full, potentially pushing White into the droppable tier once tomorrow’s official injury report is released. Stay tuned.

Headline: Jakobi Meyers (ankle) is not on Jacksonville’s final Week 11 injury report.
News Snippet: Meyers got in three limited sessions and will continue to play through this ailment. The Jaguars haven’t been tested enough to get him out of the WR4 ranks for the last few weeks, but if the Giants come to play on offense on Sunday, perhaps that will change.

Headline: Bhayshul Tuten (ankle/foot) is not on Jacksonville’s final Week 11 injury report.
News Snippet: Tuten got in a limited session on Wednesday, a DNP on Thursday while working with trainers, and appeared to do much the same on Friday before getting an official “limited” designation. Clearly gutting his way through the injury at this point, Tuten will remain a high-end RB2 against the Giants.

Headline: Treylon Burks (foot) did not practice on Friday.
News Snippet: This could just be a rest day. Burks played through the injury last week, logging just one limited session, and he was clearly limited by the injury in-game. He still has a chance to play in this week’s Monday Night Football game against the Bengals, but he would be a terribly volatile FLEX if so.

Headline: Zack Baun (back) will not play in Philadelphia’s Week 11 game against the Steelers.
News Snippet: Baun didn’t practice at any point this week and could be in rough shape for a short-week Thanksgiving game against the Cowboys as well.

Headline: Will Shipley (foot/illness) is questionable for Philadelphia’s Week 11 game against the Steelers.
News Snippet: Illness was an added designation today. While it normally probably wouldn’t matter, since Shipley is already on injured reserve, the Eagles can afford to take it slow with him if they’d like to. If active, Shipley won’t be a FLEX play with Saquon Barkley healthy.

Headline: DeVonta Smith (hamstring) is not on Philadelphia’s final Week 11 injury report.
News Snippet: He got in full sessions each of the last two days to clear the report. With Joe Milton under center, Smith is more of a WR3 than a WR2 at this point, but with six teams on bye fantasy managers can’t be choosy.

Headline: Carson Beck (back) is questionable to play in Week 11 against the Chiefs.
News Snippet: Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur told reporters earlier today that Beck is unlikely to start in Week 11 against the Chiefs, so this may just be a formality. If active, Beck would be a low-end QB2 this week despite six NFL teams being on bye. Josh Johnson is expected to start in his stead.

Headline: Dontayvion Wicks (ankle/foot) will not play in Philadelphia’s Week 11 game against the Steelers.
News Snippet: Wicks got in three limited sessions, but notably had the “foot” ailment attached to him after it only being listed as an “ankle” the last two days. It’s possible this is nothing major and the Eagles are just taking it easy with him, but a new injury should be on the radar. Wicks has little fantasy utility either way at this stage.

Headline: Jets ruled out Isaiah Williams (ribs) for Week 11 against the Chargers.
News Snippet: This is unfortunate. Williams had a chance to play a larger role with Omar Cooper (ankle) sidelined. Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell benefit from these players’ absences, though they will be catching passes thrown by a hobbled Geno Smith (ankle).

Headline: Antoine Winfield Jr. (ankle) will not play in Tampa’s Week 11 game against the Lions.
News Snippet: Winfield, who popped up with this injury on Wednesday, did not practice at any point this week. Yaya Diaby (knee) is questionable but probably on the optimistic side of it after getting in a full session on Friday. Tristan Wirfs practiced in full all week and is not on the final injury report with his toe ailment.

Headline: Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle) has been ruled out for Week 11 against the Chargers.
News Snippet: Cooper and Isaiah Williams (ribs) will both miss this week’s game, leaving Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell to lead the wide receiver corps. Both players’ target share projections should increase a tad. Cooper did not practice at all this week. He has dealt with multiple ankle injuries in his rookie season.

Headline: Baker Mayfield (foot) is questionable for Tampa Bay’s Week 11 game against the Lions.
News Snippet: Mayfield got in two limited sessions after missing Wednesday with the injury. Todd Bowles spoke to reporters earlier today and said that he was “trending in the right direction” to start this week. He seems to be on the optimistic side of questionable, Jalon Daniels would grab the start if Mayfield is unable to go.

Headline: Geno Smith (ankle) is not on the Jets’ final injury report and will play in Week 11 against the Chargers.
News Snippet: The Jets’ starting quarterback was limited on Wednesday and Thursday before upgrading to full participation on Friday. Smith has turned in a couple of decent games this season, but he’s currently on a two-game skid in which he has failed to beat 165 passing yards and/or throw a touchdown. He is stuck in the QB2 tier despite six teams being on bye this week.

Headline: D.J. Reed (hip) is questionable for Detroit’s Week 11 game against the Buccaneers.
News Snippet: He got in limited sessions all three practice days this week and seems to be trending in a good direction after missing Week 9 and Week 10 with this hip injury. He’s probably best-regarded as a game-time decision.

Headline: Cade Mays (ankle) will not play in Detroit’s Week 11 game against the Buccaneers.
News Snippet: It seems rather unlikely that Mays will be able to get up off the mat for Week 12’s Thanksgiving game as well on a short week. Juice Scruggs will continue to start for the Lions for the time being.

Headline: Chiefs ruled out RG Trey Smith (concussion) for Week 11 against the Cardinals.
News Snippet: Smith and RT Jaylon Moore (ankle) will both miss this week’s game against the Cardinals, but the Chiefs should be able to manage the situation. There is a decent overall talent gap between the two teams. Kansas City faces the Bills next week. Hopefully, the right side of the offensive line is ready for that one.

Headline: Tyjae Spears (knee) is questionable for Tennessee’s Week 11 game against the Cowboys.
News Snippet: Spears hit the questionable line with this knee injury in Week 10, Week 7 and Week 6 before this latest one. Given how similar the pathing looks to last week’s — as he also got in a full session ahead on Friday here — we think he’s more likely to play than not. He’s probably only a desperation FLEX play in a good matchup against the Cowboys busted run defense.

Headline: Carnell Tate (shoulder) is questionable for Tennessee’s Week 11 game against the Cowboys.
News Snippet: The big news here is that he got in a full session on Friday after being limited on Wednesday and Thursday. The long layoff is still a little bit concerning, but a full session likely inches him over to the optimistic side of questionable in what looks to be a shootout. Tate will have high-end WR3 appeal if he’s able to go.

Headline: Vega Ioane (shoulder/knee) is not on Baltimore’s final Week 11 injury report.
News Snippet: He got in two full sessions on Thursday and Friday. Hopefully his return will help calm down the interior of the Baltimore offensive line. The Ravens will need all the pass protection help they can get if they keep playing as they did on Monday night.

Headline: Chris Bell (knee) is not on Miami’s final Week 11 injury report.
News Snippet: He’ll play against the Bills. It’s not exactly a smash play after he missed last week’s game with some soreness in his surgically-repaired knee, but it’s certainly plausible that Bell will be in the fantasy discussion in Week 12 if he proves healthy and able this week.

Headline: Dee Alford cleared concussion protocol and is not on Buffalo’s final Week 11 injury report.
News Snippet: He’ll be tasked with slot work against the Dolphins with Christian Benford (groin) out. It’s good news for Buffalo D/ST streamers that they’ll at least have one of Buffalo’s better corners back for this one.

Headline: Caleb Douglas (shoulder) is not on Miami’s final Week 11 injury report.
News Snippet: He got in a full session to evade the questionable line on Friday. With Buffalo’s banged up secondary and the run attack sliding to a halt without Malik Willis under center, it’s plausible that Douglas can cook up some real numbers this week. He is RotoPat’s 23rd ranked receiver this week as of Friday afternoon.

Headline: Jake Ferguson (ankle/knee) will not play in Dallas’ Week 11 game against the Titans.
News Snippet: Ferguson has now missed two weeks with this injury and has not practiced at all in the interim, leaving his status for a short turnaround Week 12 highly questionable. It is wheels up in the TE2 ranks for Brevyn Spann-Ford.

Headline: Chiefs ruled out Kenneth Walker (groin) for Week 11 against the Cardinals.
News Snippet: The Chiefs face the lowly Cardinals this week, but they face the Bills next week. Allowing Walker to fully heal in time for that important matchup makes sense. Stud rookie Emmett Johnson remains a fantasy football RB1 after an explosive showing against the Falcons last week. Walker will vault back into the RB1 tier upon returning.

Headline: Raiders coach Klint Kubiak said Brock Bowers (ankle/quad) is questionable for Week 11 against the Broncos.
News Snippet: We do not yet know Bowers’ Friday participation level. He was seen at practice, and Kubiak told reporters that Bowers got “a lot of work in.” Some reports indicate that Bowers spent time away from his teammates, working with trainers, though, so he could end up being a limited participant. The Broncos struggle to cover tight ends effectively. If active, Bowers is an elite TE1, albeit with some re-injury risk.

Headline: Roman Wilson (hand) is questionable for Pittsburgh’s Week 11 game against the Eagles.
News Snippet: He got in three full sessions this week and seems likely to be activated off injured reserve — most IR activations this season have received a questionable tag regardless of how often they’ve practiced. With the depth back in their receiving corps on Sunday (assuming Michael Pittman is also activated), we’d probably fade the non DK Metcalf pass catchers against Philadelphia and see how things sort out. It’s certainly not impossible that Wilson produces real fantasy value down the stretch despite the competition.

Headline: Nick Herbig (ribs/hip) is questionable for Pittsburgh’s Week 11 game against the Eagles.
News Snippet: He did not practice at all this week, though it’s possible he’s just going to be able to play through the pain on Sunday and the Steelers are taking it easy on him. Patrick Queen (hand) is also questionable, but got in a full session on Friday and we’re optimistic about his chances of returning.

Headline: Michael Pittman (foot) is questionable for Pittsburgh’s Week 11 game against the Eagles.
News Snippet: Pittman got in two full sessions on Thursday and Friday after a limited practice on Wednesday. It would not be surprising at all if he were activated for this game ahead of Sunday, though we wouldn’t quite call it a certainty. If he does come back, he may serve more as a governor for Germie Bernard than as someone you’re excited to start in fantasy right away.

Headline: Dre Greenlaw (neck) is questionable to play in Week 11 against the Vikings.
News Snippet: We do not yet know Greenlaw’s Friday participation level. He was limited on Thursday, and the 49ers tacked on a “Not injury-related - resting player” tag to his listing. The fact that he is questionable indicates the neck injury is a factor. Perimeter CB Renardo Green (back) will play. Slot CB Upton Stout (shoulder) is questionable.

Headline: Kyler Murray (hamstring) will not play in Minnesota’s Week 11 game against the 49ers.
News Snippet: It’s his third straight week on the shelf. Carson Wentz will again handle backup duties behind Kirk Cousins.

Headline: T.J. Hockenson is not on Minnesota’s final Week 11 injury report.
News Snippet: He can be fired up as a low-end TE1 with Jordan Addison (finger) out for the foreseeable future. Hockenson got in limited practices on Wednesday and Thursday before a full session on Friday tipped him past the questionable line.

Headline: ESPN’s Mike Reiss believes signing Daniel Jones could be an option for the Patriots.
News Snippet: Drake Maye has been diagnosed with a fractured fibula and is expected to be sidelined “deep” into the regular season. Tommy DeVito replaces him as the team’s starter. He is backed up by seventh-round rookie Behren Morton, who has reportedly “made a positive impression.” Jones has played poorly this year, prompting a surprise release earlier today. Despite the poor play, Jones still might be able to outplay DeVito and the late-Day 3 rookie. Assuming Jones passes through waivers, he could make sense as an affordable bridge option for the Patriots.

Headline: CJ Donaldson (shoulder) is not on New Orleans’ final Week 11 injury report.
News Snippet: He’ll return to his pass-blocking role for the Saints, assuming they want him active, in Week 11. No fantasy value here for the moment.

Headline: Jordyn Tyson (chest) is not on New Orleans’ final Week 11 injury report.
News Snippet: He got in a full session on Friday and was cleared off the report for Week 11’s game against the Bears. He’ll be an upside WR3 after last week’s 13-target breakout against the Panthers.

Headline: Jeffery Simmons (knee) is not on Chicago’s final Week 11 injury report.
News Snippet: Simmons practiced in full on Friday after being limited with a knee listing the last two days. It wouldn’t be surprising if he continued to be limited in practice after this game given the quick turnaround to Chicago’s Week 12 Thanksgiving game against the Lions.

Headline: Kyler Gordon (shoulder) will not play in Chicago’s Week 11 game against the Saints.
News Snippet: He was ruled out after three straight missed practices following the Week 10 bye. It does not look especially likely he’ll be able to turn it around next week and play in Chicago’s Thanksgiving game against the Lions.

Headline: Kyle Monangai (toe) is not on Chicago’s final Week 11 injury report.
News Snippet: He’ll return to FLEX plausibility as the Bears take on the Saints in a game where a crockpotting run-heavy attack is certainly in the range of possibilities. Monangai has not played since Week 4, but has fully recovered from a turf toe injury and practiced in full all three days this week. He shouldn’t have any limitations.

Headline: Kyle Shanahan said Mike Evans (Achilles) was questionable for San Francisco’s Week 11 game against the Vikings.
News Snippet: We don’t have a practice status yet, but the 49ers said they’d make a decision on Evans’ status on Saturday. If active, he’ll be a reasonable WR3 bet due to the risk of in-game injury management risk and the tax the Vikings defense enacts on opposing passing games.

Headline: Saints coach Kellen Moore said Taliese Fuaga (knee) will not play in New Orleans’ Week 11 game against the Bears.
News Snippet: Asim Richards (knee) was also ruled out, leaving the Saints with 24-year-old UDFA Mason Murphy as a potential Week 11 starter at tackle.

Headline: ESPN’s Mike Reiss reports that A.J. Brown (hamstring) is expected to be sidelined for multiple weeks.
News Snippet: According to Reiss, Brown would normally be a candidate to land on injured reserve, but the Patriots are already close to the limit of how many players they can designate for return from injured reserve. The Patriots are on bye this week. Were Brown to be placed on injured reserve, he would be eligible to return for the Patriots’ Week 16 game against the Jets after missing four games. Although he will remain on the active roster, Reiss’ comments suggest Week 16 could be Brown’s expected return date. For fantasy leagues with an injured reserve spot, Brown is worth holding onto. For leagues that lack an injured reserve spot, it might make sense to drop him for a fill-in starter at the running back spot, or a player of equivalent value.

Headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Drake Maye fractured his fibula and it is expected to sideline him “deep into the regular season if he is able to return this year at all.”
News Snippet: Maye is being given the Jaxson Dart Memorial Puncher’s Chance of returning, but it doesn’t look likely that he’ll return this year and, if you were holding out hope for whatever reason, he can be dropped in most re-draft leagues at this time. Maye won’t have to undergo surgery and there was no additional ligament damage. The Patriots may choose to not put Maye on injured reserve because they are already near the limit of how many players they can designate to return.

Headline: Bills coach Joe Brady said Christian Benford (groin) will not play in Buffalo’s Week 11 game against the Dolphins.
News Snippet: Neither will Dorian Williams (calf) who also missed practice most of the week. Neither player is regarded as having a long-term injury, per Brady, so they should have a chance to get up for Week 12’s Thanksgiving game against the Chiefs.

Headline: Nnamdi Madubuike (hamstring) won’t play in Baltimore’s Week 11 game against the Panthers.
News Snippet: Madubuike did not practice all week after injuring the hamstring on Monday night. A prolonged absence wouldn’t be surprising, but the Ravens have been tight-lipped about it so far.

Headline: Giants head coach John Harbaugh said Isaiah Likely (undisclosed) is dealing with a “minor” injury.
News Snippet: Likely was noticeably absent from Friday’s practice, but Harbaugh said he expects his tight end to be okay. We assume that means he will be fine for Sunday’s game against the Jaguars, but we will need to wait to see where things stand when the team releases its final injury report on Friday. We should have a better sense of what he is dealing with soon, but in the event he can’t go, Theo Johnson would be the next man up to replace Likely.

Headline: Bills coach Joe Brady said Dalton Kincaid (thumb/ankle) is doubtful for Buffalo’s Week 11 game against the Dolphins.
News Snippet: Kincaid has not practiced yet this week and we’re guessing from this designation he won’t be heading to the field on Friday either. This has, sadly, become pretty standard for Kincaid as he simply has to be managed week-to-week on the injury report. Dawson Knox should join the TE2 ranks for Week 11 assuming Kincaid is out, though it’s plausible Kincaid’s fantasy managers can do better on the wire.

Headline: Colts head coach Shane Steichen said Anthony Richardson will start in Week 12 against the Giants.
News Snippet: The surprising release of Daniel Jones immediately thrusts Richardson back into the QB1 role, a role he hasn’t held since 2024. The former No. 4 overall pick now has a chance to make the most of what is a lost season for the Colts, who are fresh off a 26-3 loss to the Texans on Thursday night. Richardson has played sparingly this season, completing 2-of-4 passes for eight yards while rushing three times for six yards. Playing in an offense that’s devoid of weapons at receiver, the Colts would benefit from leaning into Richardson’s ability as an athlete by utilizing him in the ground game. Richardson’s rushing upside could eventually put him on the radar as a decent QB2, but we will conservatively project him as a low-end QB2/QB3 in his first start in over two years.

Headline: Colts waived QB Daniel Jones.
News Snippet: Well, the Colts apparently evaluated everything, as they said they would last night. Wow. Jones makes it 11 games into a two-year, $88 million contract. He will be subject to waivers since the trade deadline has passed. It’s possible — though we’d be hard-pressed to say likely given the $2 million owed this season, $10 million next year and $38 million in non-guaranteed 2027 cash — that someone takes a chance on the deal. If not, he’ll be free to sign anywhere for the rest of the season. Minnesota would probably take a gamble on him again after they scooped him up in this same exact manner a few years ago, but that’s just speculation on our part. It’s stunning in the sense that it happened in-season, but this was obviously the way things had been trending as Indianapolis’ offense simply hasn’t been able to operate with Jones. Anthony Richardson will take over as the starting quarterback for the time being.

Headline: Tommy Tremble (knee) is questionable for Carolina’s Week 11 game against the Ravens.
News Snippet: Tremble got in limited sessions on Thursday and Friday after missing Wednesday. He’s probably best regarded as a true question mark, though nobody’s fantasy lineup should be riding on him being inactive or not. Tremble would be a reasonable TE2 play if he were able to go.

Headline: Darren Waller (knee) is questionable for Carolina’s Week 11 game against the Ravens.
News Snippet: He got in two limited practices on Thursday and Friday. You’re probably not planning to play either he or fellow questionable tight end Tommy Tremble as anything more than a TE2 either way. If both players were somehow ruled out, Mitchell Evans would take their place in the pecking order.

Headline: Jets rule out Omar Cooper (ankle) for Week 11 against the Chargers.
News Snippet: Cooper and Isaiah Williams (ribs) will both miss this week’s game, leaving Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell to lead the wide receiver corps. Both players’ target share projections should increase a tad. Cooper did not practice at all this week. He has dealt with multiple ankle injuries in his rookie season.

Headline: Jonathon Brooks (groin) is questionable for Carolina’s Week 11 game against the Ravens.
News Snippet: Brooks practiced in full all three days this week and we’ve seen players pacing to be activated off injured reserve be given this soft questionable listing several times this year. Expect Brooks to play as Chuba Hubbard’s main backup. He’ll likely be brought along slowly in his first game back.

Headline: Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said Carson Beck (back) is unlikely to start in Week 11 against the Chiefs.
News Snippet: According to Cardinals beat writer Darren Urban, LaFleur “won’t close [the] door on Beck just yet,” but the team is preparing as if Josh Johnson will draw the start on Sunday against the Chiefs. This was already shaping up to be a disastrous matchup for the Cardinals, and an offense that is down its top three receivers, and this isn’t doing anything to help the situation. If they weren’t already doing it, fantasy managers everywhere should be scrambling to stream the Chiefs defense in what is shaping up to be a very favorable home matchup.

Headline: Rams head coach Sean McVay said “there is a possibility” Davante Adams (hamstring) plays in Week 13 against the Chiefs.
News Snippet: The Athletic’s Nate Atkins reported last week that the Rams were “hopeful” this would be the timeline for Adams’ return. McVay somewhat confirmed that optimism while speaking to the media on Friday, but noted that the star receiver isn’t “ready quite yet.” This follows McVay announcing that Puka Nacua (knee) will miss the next few months after MCL surgery, so it’s safe to assume the Rams will be thin at receiver in Week 12 when they take on the Packers on Thanksgiving Eve.

Headline: Buccaneers head coach Todd Bowles said Baker Mayfield (foot) is “trending” in the right direction to start in Week 11 against the Lions.
News Snippet: Mayfield reportedly looked good in Friday’s practice and logged back-to-back practices to close out the week. We should have an update on his official game status soon, but all signs are pointing to him starting this week against a Lions team that has allowed the fifth-most passing yards this season. We will check back in with an official update when the team provides it.

Headline: Bhayshul Tuten (ankle) was seen practicing on the side field on Friday.
News Snippet: This will presumably result in a DNP for Tuten this week, but we’ll see what the team announces when it releases its final injury report. According to Jaguars beat writer Ryan O’Halloran, Tuten was on the field with his helmet to stretch with teammates during warmups but then went to the side field. If he is listed as a DNP, it would be the second straight day Tuten failed to get on the practice field, but he could still receive a questionable designation entering the weekend. We will check back in with a final status update once the team announces it in a few hours.

Headline: Rams head coach Sean McVay said Puka Nacua will undergo surgery on his MCL and will be out “a couple months.”
News Snippet: Shortly after it was reported that Nacua “will undergo” surgery, we learned that the star receiver actually had surgery on Tuesday. We don’t know exactly how long Nacua will miss, but it’s safe to assume his only path back for the 2026 season would be if the Rams make a run in the postseason. Even then, his recovery timeline could be too long for a late-January/early-February return. The 25-year-old receiver was in the midst of another stellar season for the Rams, catching 70 passes for 715 yards and four touchdowns in the seven games he appeared in. Nacua is in the final year of his four-year rookie contract and is on track to receive a lucrative payday this offseason, presumably from the Rams. An offseason marred by off-the-field issues and a stint at a rehab facility likely delayed the decision to extend him before training camp, but Nacua continues to play at an elite level on the field. If all goes well, it sounds like he should be healed well ahead of training camp next offseason.

Headline: Baker Mayfield (foot) was spotted at Friday’s practice.
News Snippet: Mayfield will close out the week with back-to-back practices, which should give him a decent chance at playing in Week 11’s game against the Lions. Things looked doubtful for Mayfield earlier in the week, especially after the Bucs signed Cooper Rush to the practice squad on Monday. We should get official word on Mayfield’s status shortly, but it’s safe to say he is trending in the right direction at this point.

Headline: Colts head coach Shane Steichen said he will “evaluate everything” at QB after Daniels Jones’ poor outing in Week 11’s loss to the Texans.
News Snippet: Steichen didn’t commit to Jones as the Colts’ Week 12 starter for next week’s game against the Giants. Anthony Richardson replaced Jones late in Thursday night’s loss to the Texans, but the Colts have been reluctant to bench Jones, despite a disastrous season in which he has thrown for 1,974 yards, seven touchdowns, and 13 interceptions. It feels like a switch to Richardson is inevitable at some point. With some extra time to prep him for next week’s game, now could be the time to make the move back to the former No. 4 overall pick.

Headline: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said Geno Smith (ankle) is trending toward playing in Week 11 against the Chargers.
News Snippet: We should have the final word on Smith’s status shortly, but Glenn said his QB1 will log another practice on Friday, which should be enough for him to play on Sunday against the Chargers. Smith has struggled in recent weeks, throwing for 313 scoreless yards, but could have a chance to bounce back against a woeful Chargers defense that has allowed the 10th-most passing yards and the fifth-most net yards per attempt this season.

Headline: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said Isaiah Williams (ribs) will not play in Week 11 against the Chargers.
News Snippet: Williams could have been in line for a decent workload given that Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle/hip) has been ruled out, but the 25-year-old receiver will join Cooper on the sidelines for this one. Veteran Tim Patrick, who ran 22-plus routes in Weeks 5 and 6 when the Jets were shorthanded at the position, could be next in line for playing time, but he should probably be avoided even on a week with six teams on bye.

Headline: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said Omar Cooper (ankle) will not play in Week 11 against the Chargers.
News Snippet: This was to be expected. Cooper was bounced from Week 10’s game against the Bills after one snap, after he had his ankle rolled up on, and has not gotten on the practice field this week. The 22-year-old receiver has had a challenging start to his career and is now slated to miss his fifth game of the season. Fellow receiver Isaiah Williams (ribs) has also been ruled out, paving the way for Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell to have busy days against the one-win Chargers. It doesn’t sound like Cooper is at risk of being placed on injured reserve, so we’ll see if things fare any differently for him entering Week 12.

Headline: Xavier Hutchinson caught 2-of-3 targets for 13 yards in the Texans’ Week 11 win over the Colts.
News Snippet: Hutchinson’s three targets were a product of a game environment dominated by the Houston defense, with no player seeing more than the five targets accounted for by alpha wide receiver Nico Collins. Fantasy managers that were riding the recent production from Hutchinson were surely left disappointed in the down performance, with his next opportunity to return a usable fantasy outing coming in a Week 14 meeting with the Ravens. It remains to be seen whether Marvin Harrison Jr. will make it back in time for that contest, something that could influence the upside of Hutchinson in a zone-heavy matchup.

Headline: Tank Dell caught 3-of-4 targets for 27 yards in the Texans’ Week 11 win over the Colts.
News Snippet: Dell was blanked in the first half before seeing three consecutive plays drawn up for him in the third quarter, catching all of them for his complete yardage total on the evening. The team continues to take a conservative approach with the young speedster after he missed more than a year with one of the more gruesome injuries you will see, holding his fantasy value in check in the process. Dell can likely be stashed for the potential he sees his route rate increase later in the season but is likely best left on fantasy benches for the time being.

Headline: Kayshon Boutte caught both targets for 40 yards and a touchdown in the Texans’ Week 11 win over the Colts.
News Snippet: Boutte’s two targets were a product of minimal pass volume in a game the Texans were able to control with their defense. He made the most of the modest volume by coming down with a touchdown in the second quarter on a dime delivered by quarterback C.J. Stroud to the middle of the end zone from 24 yards out, catching the ball with the defender draped around his midsection. Boutte remains a shaky fantasy bet as nothing more than the third option through the air, with the team expecting to get back newcomer Marvin Harrison Jr. from a hamstring injury in short order. That could come as early as Week 12 considering the Texans now get a long week of preparation ahead of a meeting with the Ravens.

Headline: Nico Collins caught 3-of-5 targets for 58 yards and a touchdown in the Texans’ Week 11 win over the Colts.
News Snippet: Collins caught two passes, one of which went for his 42-yard touchdown, on the team’s second possession before being subject to modest pass volume due to increasingly positive game script. His touchdown grab will most certainly make an appearance on highlight reels for some time, mostly due to quarterback C.J. Stroud’s performance on the play. Stroud shrugged off a strong-side pass rusher to quickly reset his feet and deliver a strike downfield to Collins, turning a potential sack into a touchdown with the flick of his wrist. He appeared to effortlessly heave the ball 50 yards through the air without being able to step into the throw, placing the football where only Collins could catch it over the defender. Collins remains one of the league’s top talents at wide receiver but is subject to performances like this when the Texans are able to control games with their defense, which is exactly what transpired here. Up next for Collins and the Texans are the Ravens in Week 12, where the veteran receiver will remains an upside WR2 due to modest volume expectations.

Headline: David Montgomery rushed 26 times for 107 yards in the Texans’ Week 11 win over the Colts, adding 17 yards on three receptions.
News Snippet: Montgomery shook off a relatively slow start to reach 100 yards on the ground for the first time as a member of the Texans, doing so with Woody marks inactive due to a concussion. Veteran journeyman Emari Demercado handled just seven touches as the primary change of pace option. Montgomery churned out consistently positive yardage but managed just one explosive run, a 15-yard scamper to ice the game late in the fourth quarter. No longer a featured back at this point in his career, the 100-yard showing could go down as his top fantasy performance of the season with Marks expected back from injury when the Texans face the Ravens in Week 12. Treat Montgomery as a potential Flex option in that matchup.

Headline: C.J. Stroud completed 21-of-27 passes for 194 yards, three touchdowns, and one interception in the Texans’ 26-3, Week 11 win over the Colts, adding 27 yards on six carries.
News Snippet: Stroud’s lone mistake came on the team’s first possession of the game when a poorly thrown ball over the middle of the field intended for Nico Collins was picked off. He would go to work from there, completing nine of his next 10 passes while throwing two touchdowns before the half. A 17-3 lead at the break saw a slight uptick with a safety on the defense’s first time on the field in the second half, with Stroud tacking on his third touchdown throw on the following possession. The team would go into coast mode from there, eventually chasing Daniel Jones from the game with just over seven minutes remaining in the fourth quarter, with Stroud finishing with three or more touchdown passes for the fourth time in his last five appearances. Stroud and the Texans get the floundering Ravens in Week 12, where he will remain a back end QB1 in fantasy circles.

Headline: Tyler Warren caught 1-of-5 targets for 22 yards in the Colts’ Week 11 loss to the Texans.
News Snippet: The poor showing comes on the heels of a two-catch, one-yard performance in Week 10, leaving fantasy managers scratching their heads following the departures of Josh Downs and Keenan Allen at the trade deadline. Warren briefly departed in the second quarter after being shaken up on his lone reception but returned to do absolutely nothing else for the remainder of the game. The Colts gained only 165 yards of total offense with Daniel Jones under center through almost 53 minutes of play, something that has become a routine occurrence of late. Fantasy managers will want to confirm the starting quarterback ahead of a Week 12 meeting with the Giants before considering entering Warren into lineups. Even so, there appears to be no good option currently on the roster.

Headline: Ashton Dulin caught 2-of-4 targets for 30 yards in the Colts’ Week 11 loss to the Texans.
News Snippet: Both of Dulin’s receptions came on the opening possession of the game, with a 25-yard catch down the sideline sparking the drive that led to the team’s only points. The Colts remain a veritable disaster at present, leaving nobody on the weekly fantasy radar - Dulin most certainly included.

Headline: Anthony Gould caught 2-of-3 targets for 48 yards in the Colts’ Week 11 loss to the Texans.
News Snippet: Gould played sparingly despite the recent wide receiver departures, with his team-leading 48 yards more a statement on the current state of the offense than anything else. Nobody on this sinking team deserves fantasy consideration, a sentiment that extends to its depth pieces.

Headline: Jonathan Taylor rushed 11 times for 21 yards in the Colts’ Week 11 loss to the Texans, adding six yards on four receptions.
News Snippet: Taylor went as the rest of the offense went in this one, with the team gaining just 165 yards of total offense through almost 53 minutes of play with Daniel Jones under center before the veteran signal caller was replaced by Anthony Richardson. The only points mustered for the duration of the contest came on the opening possession of the game, sparked by a 25-yard completion to Ashton Dulin down the sideline. Taylor again rotated with Seth McGowan in a 1A-1B situation until the latter was forced from the game with a hamstring injury sustained on a kick return to end the first half. The team has no reason to run Taylor into the ground in a lost season, significantly capping his fantasy value in the process. Fantasy managers will want to confirm the starting quarterback for the Colts entering a Week 12 meeting with the Giants before inserting Taylor into lineups.

Headline: Daniel Jones completed 12-of-27 passes for 144 yards and an interception in the Colts’ 26-3, Week 11 loss to the Texans, adding three yards on one carry.
News Snippet: Jones led the Colts to only 165 yards of total offense through almost 53 minutes of play against the Texans, also taking a sack in the end zone for a safety, before being replaced by Anthony Richardson with just over seven minutes remaining in the fourth quarter. This is the second game in the previous four weeks in which Richardson has come on in relief of an underperforming Jones in the fourth quarter. When you add that to the continuous questions fielded by head coach Shane Steichen surrounding the quarterback position moving forward, pressure appears to be mounting toward a potential change under center in a lost season. For what it’s worth, Richardson came on and immediately threw a pass that should have been intercepted during a quick three-and-out possession, which were the only three plays he ran as the Texans controlled the ball to run out the clock. Fantasy managers should not have held on for this long, but it is safe to say that Jones can be returned to the waiver wire from whence he came.

Headline: Seth McGowan (hamstring) is questionable to return to Week 11 against the Texans.
News Snippet: McGowan pulled up lame following a kick return at the end of the first half and was deemed questionable to return when the two teams came out after the break. Jonathan Taylor appears to be in line to operate as a true workhorse for the remainder of the game after McGowan had carved out a meaningful role the previous two weeks. McGowan managed seven yards on three carries and caught his lone target for one yard prior to departing.

Headline: Anthony Gould (toe) is active for Week 11 against the Texans.
News Snippet: Gould will play through his toe injury this evening, but he is on a boom-bust WR5. The Colts are playing without both of their starting offensive tackles, and Gould is not a replacement-level starter.

Headline: NFL on Prime’s James Palmer reports that the Colts want their next general manager to have a say in Jonathan Taylor and Daniel Jones’ futures with the team.
News Snippet: The Colts have faced scrutiny for their decision to keep Taylor and Jones on the roster, rather than trading one or both away for draft picks. Palmer said this is about empowering their next general manager. The team has reportedly compiled a preliminary list of candidates, potentially putting the team in position to make a hire quickly after the season. Stay tuned.

Headline: T.J. Hockenson (wrist) was limited on Thursday.
News Snippet: Hockenson has a chance to return from his wrist injury for the Vikings’ Week 11 game against the 49ers. It would be nice to see him upgrade to full participation tomorrow. If active, Hockenson will likely qualify as a low-end TE1 with six NFL teams on bye this week.

Headline: Caleb Douglas (shoulder) was limited on Thursday.
News Snippet: Douglas is still limited despite coming off the Dolphins’ Week 10 bye, but he has a chance to play this week against the Bills. He will be catching passes thrown by Kyle McCord, but with six teams on bye, Douglas is at least in the FLEX conversation this week.

Headline: Chris Bell (knee) was limited on Thursday.
News Snippet: Bell reportedly hyperextended his knee last week, hence his day-to-day labeling this week. Bell had been limited from time to time already this year by soreness in his surgically repaired knee. The fact that this is unrelated is actually good news. He has a chance to play in Week 11 against the Bills.

Headline: Colts declared CB Sauce Gardner, QB Riley Leonard, TE Will Mallory, LT Bernhard Raimann, DT Jerry Tillery, RT Jalen Travis and CB Charvarius Ward inactive for Week 11 against the Texans.
News Snippet: Gardner and Ward are the Colts’ starting perimeter cornerbacks, and Raimann and Travis are the Colts’ starting offensive tackles. Losing all four for this game will be consequential. The Texans’ wide receivers and pass rushers should play efficiently in this week’s Thursday Night Football game.

Headline: Texans declared Marvin Harrison, EDGE Danielle Hunter, RB Woody Marks, TE Brevin Jordan, C Jake Andrews, OG Wyatt Teller and OT Nate Thomas inactive for Week 11 against the Colts.
News Snippet: Harrison (hamstring) and Marks (concussion) are both out this week, condensing the Texans’ skill position corps for fantasy football purposes. Both players can be stashed on benches in 12-team leagues, though neither player is a must-stash option. David Montgomery should handle a sizable workload with Marks out.

Headline: Ladd McConkey (back) was limited on Thursday.
News Snippet: The Chargers’ No. 1 wide receiver is tentatively on track to play in Week 11 against the Jets, but ideally he will upgrade to full participation tomorrow. The Chargers have been willing to run the passing offense through McConkey when he is active. He is a WR2, albeit with some re-injury risk, if he suits up.

Headline: Mike Evans (Achilles) was limited on Thursday.
News Snippet: Evans has a chance to play in Week 11 against the Vikings. If active, Evans should be in fantasy football lineups. Re-injury risk is possible, but the 49ers have handled this issue smartly. We should have a decent indication as to whether he will make his return by tomorrow evening. Stay tuned.

Headline: Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) was limited on Thursday.
News Snippet: Wicks is stuck in the questionable column, but he still has a chance to play. With QB3 Joe Milton at the helm, Wicks would only be a WR4/5 against the Steelers in Week 11. He does not need to be rostered in 12-team leagues.

Headline: Will Shipley (foot) was limited on Thursday.
News Snippet: Shipley could need another week to fully recover from his injured reserve-worthy foot injury. Shipley partially tore his plantar fascia just over a month ago. Once he is active, he will likely serve as the Eagles’ No. 2 running back.

Headline: Zack Baun (back) did not practice on Thursday.
News Snippet: Baun is on the wrong side of questionable for the Eagles’ Week 11 game against the Steelers. If he is unable to play, the Steelers’ rushing attack should have a slightly easier time moving the ball. Stay tuned.

Headline: DeVonta Smith (hamstring) practiced in full on Thursday.
News Snippet: Excellent news. The Eagles’ No. 1 wide receiver is on track to face the Steelers in Week 11. Although he will be trying to catch passes from erratic QB Joe Milton, Smith’s target volume should keep him in the WR2 tier. It is possible that the team keeps him on a snap count, but he will be featured when he is on the field.

Headline: Isaiah Williams (ribs) did not practice on Thursday.
News Snippet: Williams’ injury is unfortunate because Omar Cooper (ankle) is seemingly unlikely to play. If Williams were able to go this weekend, he would enter the boom-bust FLEX tier with six NFL teams on bye. Hopefully, he practices tomorrow.

Headline: Omar Cooper (ankle/hip) did not practice on Thursday.
News Snippet: The Jets’ rookie wide receiver is on the wrong side of questionable. He appears to be likely to miss this week’s game against the Chargers. Ankle issues have bothered him for some time. Perhaps taking a week off would benefit him in the long run. He remains a worthwhile hold at this time.

Headline: Geno Smith (ankle) was limited on Thursday.
News Snippet: Smith is tentatively on track to play in the Jets’ Week 11 game against the Chargers, though his mobility could be somewhat impacted if this is indeed the case. Smith would warrant QB2 treatment if active. He is backed up by Cade Klubnik.

Headline: Carson Beck (back) was added to the injury report as a limited participant on Thursday.
News Snippet: Beck’s back issues continue. The rookie quarterback has dealt with this for weeks now. He should be viewed as questionable to play in the Cardinals’ Week 11 game against the Chiefs. Journeyman QB Josh Johnson is his backup.

Headline: Brock Bowers (ankle/quad) was limited on Thursday.
News Snippet: Bowers resumed practicing in a limited capacity today, and although his quad ailment was not reported early in the week, it is not new. The Raiders listed him with both ankle and quad injuries yesterday as well, which likely explains why Bowers had such a hard time returning to the Raiders’ Week 10 loss to the Seahawks. He is tentatively on track to face the Broncos this weekend.

Headline: Packers released RB Pierre Strong.
News Snippet: We take this move as a good sign for Josh Jacobs’ (finger) health. Strong could end up being signed to the Packers’ practice squad. He played a rotational role for Green Bay this season, leading the team with 17 opportunities in Week 6.

Headline: Antoine Winfield (ankle) did not practice on Thursday.
News Snippet: The Buccaneers’ stud safety is trending toward a Week 11 absence. His team faces the Lions this week. Fortunately, Buccaneers LT Tristan Wirfs (toe) is practicing in full and should be good to go.

Headline: Ray Davis (hamstring) did not practice on Thursday.
News Snippet: Davis is still worth stashing on benches in 12-team leagues. He is James Cook’s primary backup. Passing down specialist Ty Johnson (knee) is practicing in full this week and should be good to go.

Headline: Christian Benford (groin) did not practice on Thursday.
News Snippet: Benford and Bills LB Dorian Williams (calf) remained sidelined today. Bills slot CB Dee Alford (concussion) resumed practicing in a limited capacity, but he is still firmly in the questionable camp. The Bills can probably sneak past the Dolphins if a few of their defenders are absent, but having them on the field is obviously ideal.

Headline: Dalton Kincaid (thumb/ankle) did not practice on Thursday.
News Snippet: This is a little concerning. Backup plans should be made at this time. Kincaid played through the ankle injury in Week 10 against the Jets, but evidently picked up a thumb injury along the way. Dawson Knox would only be a TE2 if Kincaid sits, but the Dolphins’ defense is hardly imposing.

Headline: Dalton Risner (knees) did not practice on Thursday.
News Snippet: The Bengals’ stud right guard is dealing with injuries to both knees. Hopefully, the extra day of rest leading up to this week’s Monday Night Football game allows him to get healthy enough to play. The offense is better with him active.

Headline: Andrei Iosivas (thumb) is practicing in full for Week 11 against the Commanders.
News Snippet: Iosivas is seemingly on track to play in Week 11’s Monday Night Football game against the Commanders, but he does not need to be rostered in 12-team formats. Ja’Marr Chase, Tee Higgins (knee), Chase Brown and Mike Gesicki are playing very well in the receiving game.

Headline: Tee Higgins (knee) is practicing in full for Week 11 against the Commanders.
News Snippet: Higgins injured his knee in Week 10 against the Steelers, but apparently it is only a minor injury. The Bengals’ No. 2 wide receiver is having an excellent season, and that top-tier performance should continue against a beatable Commanders’ pass defense. Higgins is a borderline WR1/2 with six teams on bye.

Headline: Joe Burrow (illness) is practicing in full for Week 11 against the Commanders.
News Snippet: Burrow should be able to face the Commanders in this week’s Monday Night Football game without issue. Fortunately, his No. 2 wide receiver, Tee Higgins (knee), is also practicing in full this week. Burrow is an elite QB1.

Headline: Jordyn Tyson (chest) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
News Snippet: It’s back-to-back limited sessions for Tyson, leaving him likely on the optimistic side of questionable heading into Friday’s practice sessions. Tyson will be an upside WR3 against the Bears in Week 11 based on the volume he was commanding last week so long as he avoids any unexpected setbacks on Friday.

Headline: Vega Ioane (shoulder/knee) practiced in full on Thursday.
News Snippet: The Ravens’ talented rookie guard continues to practice and play through two difficult injuries. Ravens DT Nnamdi Madubuike (hamstring) remains sidelined through two Week 11 practices. Ioane should be able to face the Panthers this weekend. Madubuike could be sidelined.

Headline: Jakobi Meyers (ankle) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
News Snippet: Meyers has been rolling through this ankle issue the last few weeks and the fact that he remains limited shouldn’t be considered worrisome. He’ll be a fringe WR3 with six teams on bye in Week 11.

Headline: Chris Rodriguez (hand) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
News Snippet: Rodriguez has now gotten in back-to-back limited sessions. The veteran backup would slide into an enviable spot if Bhayshul Tuten were unable to go after Tuten’s Thursday DNP, but we’d be surprised if it wound up that way after Tuten played through these injuries the last few weeks. If Tuten is active, Rodriguez is just a rough FLEX play, even with six teams on bye.

Headline: Bhayshul Tuten (ankle/foot) did not practice on Thursday.
News Snippet: He was spotted on the sideline with trainers, and he has played through this injury each of the last two weeks. That makes us optimistic that a rug pull won’t be forthcoming on Friday. Still, the Friday practice participation line has yet to be written and it is a negative trend after Wednesday’s limited session.

Headline: Carnell Tate (shoulder) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
News Snippet: Tate has now gotten in back-to-back limited sessions, though the fact that he’s coming off three weeks lost (two games, bye) leaves us a little unsure if we should say he’s “trending” towards playing. A full session would be nice to see and we’d be surprised if he cleared the questionable line on Friday without one.

Headline: Tyjae Spears (knee) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
News Snippet: It’s an upgrade from a Wednesday DNP. The Cowboys/Titans game has been looking like it’ll be a shootout if the Titans can keep up their end of the bargain, and six teams are on bye. Even with that, we still can’t muster much FLEX excitement for Spears as Tony Pollard’s backup.

Headline: Nick Herbig (ribs/hip) did not practice on Thursday.
News Snippet: Herbig is on the wrong side of questionable for the Steelers’ Week 11 game against the Eagles. Hopefully, he can get healthy before long. Patrick Queen (hand) remains limited, but he is on track to play this weekend.

Headline: Kenneth Walker (groin) did not practice on Thursday.
News Snippet: It’s looking like it will be another RB1 ranking for Emmett Johnson against the Cardinals this week. Walker has not been on the field for either of the first two practices of the week and if there’s a coach on the team or a #SourcedMen claiming he has a real chance to play, we haven’t seen it yet.

Headline: Michael Pittman (foot) practiced in full on Thursday.
News Snippet: Pittman is tentatively on track to return in time for the Steelers’ Week 11 game against the Eagles. In his three games played from Weeks 1-3, Pittman caught seven passes for 89 yards. He will only be a WR4/5 when he returns to the field, though the Steelers do not currently have a starting wide receiver who is reliably producing. It is possible for him to carve out a role in the coming weeks.

Headline: Treylon Burks (foot) is practicing in full ahead of Washington’s Week 11 game with the Bengals.
News Snippet: Burks missed Week 9 and played through this injury in Week 10, and it seems like the extra rest after Thursday Night Football has done him some good. If he can overtake Chig Okonkwo as the No. 2 target in Washington’s passing game down the stretch, perhaps there’s some reasonable fantasy value to be had.

Headline: Chig Okonkwo (back) is practicing in full ahead of Washington’s Week 11 game with the Bengals.
News Snippet: Okonkwo left last Thursday night’s game against the Giants briefly with an injury scare, but had returned by the end of the game. This listing tells us he’s in no danger of missing Monday Night Football and, assuming Ben Sinnott isn’t suddenly usurping him as the starter after his nice game, Okonkwo can be played as a fringe TE1.

Headline: Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) is practicing in full ahead of Washington’s Week 11 game with the Bengals.
News Snippet: Pretty much all the smoke here is that he’ll be activated and ready to go for Monday Night Football and the injury report does not disagree with that assertion. We’re expecting to see him as questionable on the final injury report because that is just generally how teams label players returning from IR, but ‘Bill’ is looking like a reasonable FLEX play against the Bengals.

Headline: Jordan Schultz reports the Saints plan to release S Justin Reid at his request.
News Snippet: Reid’s having his worst season in the league per PFF’s charting data, having compiled a 49.1 PFF defensive grade and his second-worst coverage grade as a pro at 47.8. That said, Reid has plenty of versatility and wants to seek work with a contender. It sounds like he’ll likely find a new home in the near future.

Headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports that Puka Nacua will serve a three-game suspension for violating the league’s personal conduct policy while on injured reserve.
News Snippet: Schefter notes that the timing of Nacua’s suspension “could potentially save him a substantial amount of money.” Suspended players are not paid, and Nacua is in the final year of his rookie contract. Serving the suspension now “will cost him a lot less than serving it on his next contract, which is expected to be far more lucrative.” Schefter does not say whether he thinks the Rams will be the team that pays him, but a big payday is apparently still expected. Players are required to miss four games on injured reserve. Nacua has already missed one game. The Rams are on bye this week. He will spend the remainder of his injured reserve stint while also serving his suspension, and he will be eligible to return for Week 15 against the Cowboys. Nacua will be allowed to rehab his injuries at the Rams’ facility for the suspension’s final two weeks.

Headline: Kyler Gordon (shoulder) did not practice on Thursday.
News Snippet: Gordon, the Bears’ starting slot cornerback, is on the wrong side of questionable for this week’s game against the Saints. Bears DT Jeffery Simmons was limited by a knee injury, but DC Dennis Allen said he does not expect the injury to impact Simmons’ availability.

Headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter believes that the Titans or Chargers would host “an auction” for the 2027 NFL Draft’s No. 1 overall pick if either team gets it.
News Snippet: The Titans are currently in position to receive the No. 1 overall pick, and the Chargers are right behind them. Schefter spent much of the segment discussing the Titans, who Schefter says have “enough conviction” in Cam Ward that they would pass on the opportunity to draft Oklahoma State QB Drew Mestemaker. He cites the Dolphins, Jets, Cardinals and Browns as potential suitors. Poor play from Ward could still change minds in the Titans’ front office, but for now, it seems as though his job is secure.

Headline: Tommy Tremble (knee) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
News Snippet: Tremble, who had 48 yards last week against the Saints, is probably the preferred TE2 play between himself and Darren Waller if both players make it to Sunday’s game against the Ravens healthy. Each of them logged a limited session on Thursday after missing Wednesday.

Headline: Darren Waller (knee) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
News Snippet: He didn’t practice Wednesday, so this is a good sign for his availability. With Tommy Tremble also practicing though, we may remain in the Panthers TE Stasis where both players are taking too much volume off the table for you to want to start either of them in fantasy leagues.

Headline: Brock Bowers (ankle) resumed practicing on Thursday.
News Snippet: This is great to see.
